A slice that folded them into one anchor would have shipped a block refusing a Poison the card does not refuse. **AND THE COUNT WAS A FLOOR RATHER THAN A TOTAL**: §D134's census was `LIKE '%Flip a coin. the pipeline still RUNS (Weakness is computed and reported) and the block nulls the RESULT, so it SUPERSEDES rather than stacks. **IN, effects half (the WIDER reading only):** §12 Special Conditions on the body, the §11 retreat rider, an Energy discarded off it, the destination half of a counter MOVE, and — the sharpest — **damage COUNTERS PUT on it**, because this engine has ruled since D138/D139 that a placement is not attack damage (it skips Weakness, Resistance and every reduction passive), so it falls **entirely** on the effects side and a **NARROW block does not stop it**. **OUT:** anything an attack does to a **different** Pokémon (one Spread Shot declaration is prevented on the shielded Active and lands 20 on every benched body); anything done to the **PLAYER** rather than to a Pokémon (a mill, a hand disruption); the attacker's own recoil and the §9 counterattack (done to the ATTACKER); and **everything that is not an ATTACK** — a Trainer, an activated or triggered Ability, a §13 Checkup tick. **⚠️ THE STATE IS A TURN STAMP, AND THE REASON IS NOT D124's — THIS IS THE HEADLINE.** D124 chose a stamp to avoid a boundary clear a future slice could forget; here **the boundary clear that already exists is actively WRONG**. D112's `retreatBlocked` reuses §13.4's paralysis clock (cleared in `runCheckup` for `endedSeat`) and that works because the retreat block sits on the **DEFENDER's** body. **This one sits on the INSTALLER's OWN**, so the very first Checkup after the attack has `endedSeat` = the holder's seat and the same clear **lifts the block a full turn EARLY, before its window has opened at all** — two shapes that look identical in a doc and are mirror images in the code. `InPlayPokemon.attackBlock: { turn: number; effects: boolean } | null` therefore stamps **`state.turn + 1`** (declaring an attack ENDS the turn per §5.3, so the next turn is the opponent's *by construction* — no seat is stored and none is needed) and expires **by arithmetic**, with nothing anywhere to clear it and the stale stamp deliberately left sitting on the card. **Measured: reusing D112's clock fails 12 tests; stamping the installing turn instead of the next one fails the same 12.** **⚠️ "EFFECTS OF ATTACKS" IS A PROVENANCE THE TARGET CANNOT ANSWER, SO IT RIDES `EffectContext.invokedBy?: "attack"` — AND THIS REFINES D139 RATHER THAN REVERSING IT.** D139 explicitly declined a context field and put the provenance on the OP (`damageActive`/`damageChosen` still carry `source`, and still should) because a **LOG LABEL** is a property of the row an op emits. What rides on the CONTEXT is a **RULE that SIX ops must answer identically**, and the only site that knows the answer is the one that started the program: written per op it would be one fact in six places with six chances to go stale. D139's second objection — that `ctx` is serialized into every park — is exactly what makes it right here: an attack effect that PARKS and resolves three actions later is still an attack's effect, and an old continuation lacking the field reads as "not an attack", which is byte-identically the pre-slice behaviour. **The two provenances are PINNED TO AGREE** on every producer in the pool. Without the check Crushing Hammer and Boss's Orders stop working inside the window; the sharpest witness is **Trevenant's between-turns Ability reaching the SAME `damageActive` op an attack reaches**, firing at the Checkup that ends the window turn where `state.turn` is still the block's own number and only `invokedBy` can save it. **⚠️ `effects` IS A FIELD — D131's widen-don't-add rule applied and PASSING (the D139 case, not D138's)**: same install site, holder, stamp, event, expiry and three early clears, and the suite asserts the two derived programs are **byte-identical once the one field is stripped**. OPTIONAL, with the polarity deliberate (D135's `zone` from the other end): the printed words WIDEN the block, so a producer that forgets it blocks **LESS** rather than more. **NOT widened to a `damage` flag**, with the warranting condition written down — Palafin `sv03-145`'s effects-WITHOUT-damage reading, ONE printing on a different sentence. **⚠️ THE EARLY CLEARS ARE §10's, AND WHICH ONE IS REACHABLE IS INVERTED FROM D112's**: the **EVOLVE** clear is **unreachable by construction** (installing ends the turn, the window is the opponent's, nobody evolves on someone else's turn) and is written anyway with a surgery pinning the rule, while the **SWITCH** clear is reachable in the sharpest possible way — a **Boss's Orders played INSIDE the window** drags the shielded body off the spot and the protection goes with it, pinned by a following Spread Shot landing **20 on the very body that was immune a moment earlier**. Both stay SILENT (the `POKEMON_SWITCHED`/`POKEMON_EVOLVED` row tells the story — D112's own call). **⚠️ THE ONLY WAY TO KNOCK OUT A SHIELDED POKÉMON is a counter PUT through the NARROW reading** — the wide one refuses the placement and the damage half refuses every hit — driven end to end (`COUNTERS_PLACED` < `KNOCKED_OUT` < `PRIZES_OWED` to the attacker). **⚠️ TWO NEW EVENTS, AND THE VOICE IS THE MIRROR OF D141's**: `ATTACK_BLOCK_APPLIED { seat, uid, effects }` renders in the **ACTIVE** voice — `seat` owns the shielded Pokémon **and** that Pokémon is the ACTOR's own, where `RETREAT_BLOCKED`'s seat owns the victim and D141's causer is the other player — with deliberately **no `…_ENDED` twin** (a stamp expires with nothing to announce, and manufacturing a row would reintroduce the per-turn scan the stamp exists to avoid); `ATTACK_EFFECT_PREVENTED { seat, uid }` fires **once per refused op**, because a silently-skipped attack clause reads exactly like a bug. The damage half needs no event — `DAMAGE_DEALT.prevented` has named that FACT since Safeguard (0.58.0). **⚠️ `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` 3 → 4, AND IT IS D124's CASE RATHER THAN D140's**: no `EffectOp` moved at all; what moved is a **new REQUIRED field on `InPlayPokemon`**, so every Pokémon in play in an old record lacks it — and it would read back **BENIGNLY** (`undefined.turn` is never `state.turn`, and no such block could have been installed by a deploy with no op to install one), which is exactly the soft landing that constant exists to refuse. `EffectContext.invokedBy` is OPTIONAL and therefore a WIDENING (D125's distinction), asked about explicitly rather than folded in. **⚠️ THE GUARD IS SWEPT, NOT LISTED (D140's move)**: the suite DISCOVERS every op kind any attack in `FIXTURE_POOL` can produce — walking `coinFlipGate` bodies, since this whole family hides inside one — and asserts the §11 classification is **TOTAL over the discovered set in BOTH directions**, so a slice that teaches the deriver a new op fails there until it has said which side of the reading that op falls on. **Cost: 1 op member + impl, 1 state field + type, 1 `continuous.ts` reader (`attackBlockOf`), 2 events, 2 log arms, 2 regexes, 2 deriver arms, 1 `EffectContext` field, 6 guarded effect sites, 4 damage sites, 3 early clears, `preventBlock.test.ts` (32 tests) on its own `PREVENT_BLOCK_DECK`, 2 fixtures (Scyther `sv03-004` — the wide reading with a printed 10, a D125 tail board; Chosen over `ENERGY_DISCARDED`'s `actor` field because it costs no event field and the producing `ATTACK_DECLARED` row already names the actor directly above. **⚠️ 2 (low) — THREE REGEXES MISSED THE `['’]` CLASS, AND TWO SUITES HAD PINNED THE GAP AS INTENDED.** `ATTACK_COIN_MILL_PRINTED`, `ATTACK_COIN_MILL_UNTIL_TAILS` (D130) and `OPPONENT_ACTIVE_TYPE_CLAUSE` (D120) spelled `opponent's` straight-only while every sibling on the SAME noun phrase carries the class `effects.ts` documents as existing "so a re-ingest changing only punctuation cannot silently un-derive" the sentence. **The ASYMMETRY is the defect**: a U+2019 re-ingest would keep D131's mills deriving while D130's two dropped to the loud path — a regression reading as "two cards broke". **AND THE TESTS ASSERTED THE BUG**: `perHeadsProgram.test.ts` listed both curly variants as must-be-REFUSED near-misses while commenting they "would silently drop both cards onto the loud path with no number to notice it by", and `typeNameClause.test.ts` pinned Wonder Flash's bytes while observing a curly apostrophe "would silently un-map the clause". Both moved to POSITIVE assertions of **equality with the straight form**; the byte-pins stay (they say what the catalog holds, the new tests say the reader does not depend on it). **⚠️ 3 (low, latent) — THE TRUNCATION GUARD HAD NO READER, AND CLOSING IT COST THE ENGINE'S FIRST `throw`.** `rng.ts` returns faces "precisely so a caller can detect the truncation" and no caller did, so a truncated all-heads sequence would quietly score **64 heads**. Guard placed in `takeFlips`, the single choke point for the `untilTails` arm. **The engine has zero other throws and is total by design** — taken because there is no honest value to return, and unreachable by construction so it cannot fire today. **Deliberately untested**: driving it needs `vi.mock` on the RNG, which this suite has never used and which breaks a stronger convention than the throw does. **⚠️ NOT DONE — the LITERAL CLAUSE-TABLE KEYS have the same U+2019 exposure** (~8 exact `Map` lookups); a Map key cannot carry a character class, so the fix is a normalisation pass at lookup — a design call, left out rather than expanded into silently. **THE GENERALISATION IS ABOUT THE LOOP, NOT THE CODE: A SUITE WRITTEN BY THE SESSION THAT WROTE THE CODE INHERITS ITS BLIND SPOT.** Both low findings are places where the author saw the hazard, wrote it down, and asserted the wrong side of it — which is why `/code-review` belongs on a CADENCE rather than at the end. Engine version UNCHANGED (no behaviour a card can reach moved); no `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` bump, no web/API/DB/schema diff. > ### ▶ AND THE TWO RULES D416 EARNED
>
> 🛑 **(1) A GUARD THAT ONLY EVER RUNS ON THE FORCED PATH DOES NOT GUARD THE PARKED ONE.**
> `parkOrForce` auto-resolves at ONE candidate, so a suite whose boards all field one candidate
> exercises the forced arm exclusively — and every assertion still passes, which is why it reads as
> covered. D416's marker on the `applyChoice` path had **no witness at all**, and only a mutant found
> it. ⚠️ **WHEN AN OP CAN PARK, COUNT THE CANDIDATES YOUR BOARDS ACTUALLY OFFER.** If none of them
> offers two, the park is untested no matter how many cases there are.
>
> 🛑 **(2) COPYING A FUNCTION COPIES ITS MUTANTS' ANCHORS, AND THE CORPUS GOES QUIET RATHER THAN
> RED.** Writing the new funnel by copying `gustTargets` made three D331 rows match TWO sites —
> `find occurs 2×`, D404's wrong-arm trap. `precheck` catches it mechanically, **but only if you run
> it**; a whole-corpus sweep would have reported a phantom verdict about the wrong function.
> ⚠️ **AND THE REPAIR IS TWO-SIDED**: re-anchoring the old rows onto lines the original uniquely owns
> leaves the COPY untested unless you also write rows for it. Do both, or you have moved a tested
> line into a file nothing pins.

> `parkOrForce`, which gives the M1 doctrine for free: **0 candidates = silent no-op, 1 = forced, ≥2 =

> ### ▶ THE FIVE THINGS TO CARRY FORWARD ABOVE EVERYTHING ELSE
>
> 🛑 **(1) WHEN A PRINTED NOUN PHRASE HAS TWO LIVE READINGS, THE ENGINE'S OWN EXISTING ANSWER
> DECIDES — NOT TASTE, AND NOT THE SIMPLER CODE.** *"The Retreat Cost of your opponent's Active
> Pokémon"* could have meant `retreatCostOf` (the printed {C} column) or `effectiveRetreatCost`
> (the board fold, D322). Both were implemented, both had consumers, and they disagree on any board
> with a retreat Stadium or a retreat aura. **THE DECIDING FACT WAS NOT IN THE SENTENCE, IT WAS IN
> `attack.ts`**: `DamageCountSource.opponentActiveRetreatCost` (D110) has read the SAME printed noun
> phrase through the fold since 0.61.0, so a printed reading would have made one phrase mean two
> things in one file — D159, applied to a NOUN PHRASE rather than to a mechanism. ⚠️ **THE GENERAL
> MOVE: BEFORE ARGUING FROM THE RULES, GREP FOR THE PHRASE AND SEE WHETHER THIS ENGINE HAS ALREADY
> ANSWERED IT.** That took one grep and settled a question the handoff had budgeted a whole slice for.

> drives the fold LARGER (a printed-{C} defender folding to {C}{C}) and §4 drives it SMALLER (a
> printed-{C}{C} defender folding to {C} under Beach Court). **§3 ALONE IS GREEN UNDER A BUILD THAT
> READ `printed + 1`** — a reading nobody would defend, but one that a one-directional ladder cannot

> driven disagreement. **COPY THIS SHAPE FOR ANY FUTURE TWO-READING CLAUSE.**

### Prior resume point (P4 3c-vii-a — the spectator redaction, kept for continuity)
**P4 increment 3c-vii-a is DONE (online.md, D78) — the spectator REDACTION, the hidden-information half of
spectate.** `redactGame(state, side, spectating)` withholds both hands, both sides' setup placements and
every actor affordance, through ONE `actor = spectating ? null : phase.seat` gate that reuses the guards the
five `turn:action` helpers already had. The threat model is a PLAYER watching their own match, so the sides
are symmetric and the property is "a spectator sees strictly less than either player". 1858 → **1865** tests;
`bun run check` green. **It has NO CALLER yet** — which is the whole of the next slice.

**Next concrete action — 3c-vii-b: wire spectate up.** It is scoped to need **no new frame and no new URL —
the lobby link IS the spectate link**:
1. **DO.** `helloDecision` already returns `reject-full` for a third player. In that branch, IF the lobby is
   `in-game`, also mark the socket a spectator (a marker in `attachment.ts`; no `PlayerState`, nothing added
   to the snapshot, so the lobby reducer is untouched) and send it `redactGame(state, "p1", true)`. Then
   `broadcastMatch` includes spectator sockets alongside seated ones. The rule to hold: **you can watch a
   MATCH, you cannot watch a lobby** — outside in-game, `reject-full` stays the dead end it is today.
2. **Client.** `useLobby` sets a sticky `rejected` flag on `reject` and then DROPS every `match` frame
   (`if (rejected) break`), so it needs a distinct `spectating` status that keeps the connection and accepts
   the board. `OnlineMatch` needs a read-only mode: no `OnlineHud`, no Concede, no Rematch, no drags — the
   game LOG should stay, since following the game is the point. `LobbyRoom`'s `status === "full"` InfoScreen
   is where the fork lives.
3. **Decide first:** are the two players TOLD someone is watching? Not telling them is less code and matches
   how the lobby already treats a refused socket (silence); telling them needs a spectator COUNT on the
   snapshot, which is a wire change and a broadcast on every join/leave. Recommend: silent for now, and say
   so out loud in the docs rather than leaving it unasked.
4. **Then browser-verify** with a third profile on the same lobby code, checking the thing the unit tests
   cannot: that the spectator's board renders and updates live, and that neither hand appears in it.

**P4 increment 3c-iv is DONE (online.md, D75) — a mid-match LEAVE now FORFEITS the match instead of voiding

leave and the 90s timeout are one code path), then commits a lobby change that KEEPS the seat while in-game
(the new pure `applyBye`) — because freeing it would take the lobby out of in-game, drop `MATCH_KEY` and blank
the winner's board a frame after telling them they'd won. The rule is total on purpose (both slots, live AND
finished game), which is what makes it safe against the TWO `bye` frames a real leave sends. Client-side,
`BackToMenu` now takes an overridable `LeaveConfirmCopy` (via `PlaymatView.leaveConfirm`) so the online Back
button warns that leaving forfeits. 1835 → **1841** tests; `bun run check` green. **BROWSER-VERIFIED on two
real clients, both directions** (host-leaves and guest-leaves): the player who stayed got "You win! / The
match was forfeited." at once, kept their board, and was never dropped to the waiting screen; the Back dialog
showed the forfeit warning under a real hit-tested click; zero page errors. Worth doing because the DO class
has no tests at all — `applyBye` is unit-tested, the `bye` → `concedeSeat` wiring is not.

**Next concrete action — 3c-v: the opponent-facing forfeit COUNTDOWN.** With 3c-iv landed, the only path that
still leaves a player waiting in silence is an UNGRACEFUL drop (crash / killed tab / dead network — the 3c-ii
clock): their opponent sees nothing at all for 90s, not even that the seat went quiet. The shape:
1. **Put the deadline on the wire.** It belongs on the LOBBY SNAPSHOT, not the `match` frame: the arming
   moment (the disconnect grace expiring in `alarm()`) already commits a snapshot, no `match` frame is sent
   there, and a snapshot reaches a reconnecting client for free. Suggested `PlayerState.forfeitAt?: number |
   null` — **optional on the wire**, so a snapshot persisted by the PREVIOUS deploy (SNAPSHOT_KEY has no
   version gate, unlike `MatchRecord` since 3c-i) still parses instead of killing the lobby.
2. **Consider making it the single source of truth** — i.e. drop `ABANDON_KEY` and read the deadlines off the
   snapshot's seats in `scheduleMaintenance`/`forfeitAbandoned`, clearing them where the hello branches
   already set `connected: true` (`seatGuest` reconnect / `reseatHost` / `createSnapshot`). Mirroring the
   deadline into the snapshot while `ABANDON_KEY` stays authoritative would be two sources that can drift.
   Note 3c-ii's lesson: the DO class itself has NO tests, so anything that must be *scheduled* to work is
   invisible to the suite — re-check `scheduleMaintenance` by hand.
3. **Render it**: a small ticking banner in `OnlineMatch` while the game is live and the opponent's seat is
   disconnected ("Opponent disconnected — forfeits in 0:45"), counting off the server epoch ms the way

### Prior resume point (P4 increment 3a + 3a-sec — real deck selection + seat authentication, kept for continuity)
**P4 increment 3a (real deck selection at the match handoff) is DONE (online.md, D69).** The lobby loads
each player's OWN chosen deck from D1 — the first AUTHENTICATED surface in an otherwise account-less lobby.
**Increment 3 is SPLIT:** 3a (this — resolution + the failure surface), 3b (the online ability + non-Stadium
trainer HUD), 3c+ (reconnect/timeouts, concede/rematch, spectate). The `/ws` upgrade resolves the forwarded
`session` cookie → a per-socket userId (`resolveUserIdFromCookie`, DO-only, `attachUserId`); the handoff
reads each deck OWNER-SCOPED (`loadPlayerDeck` — `WHERE decks.id = <client deckId> AND decks.userId = <the
socket's authenticated userId>`), so a crafted `select-deck` for another user's deck resolves to nothing and
an anonymous socket is refused. Contents come from D1, never the client, so no forged 60. On failure the
alarm `resetAfterFailedStart` (back to selecting) + broadcasts `{kind:"match-error"}` — the load-failure
wedge is closed. `FIXED_MATCH_DECKS` removed. **3a-sec (seat authentication) folded in:** a playerId, once
claimed by an account, can only be re-adopted by that account (`seatClaimAllowed` + a DO-only

their own bound seat — the intended boundary, low-probability (30-day sessions; a browser that drops the

same-tab account SWITCH is locked out for the lobby's lifetime (recoverable in a new tab — fresh playerId);

cleared by the empty-lobby `deleteAll`).

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 the ANY-target snipe family with conditional W/R — D59, kept for continuity)
**The ANY-target snipe family is live, with conditional W/R (P3-M5, D59), engine 0.39.0.**
"This attack does N damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon." (the WHOLE attack — the Active
OR a Bench) now SIMULATES. `damageChosen` gained `target: "opponentAny"` (candidates = the
opponent's Active + Bench, via `oppAnyRefs`) and `placeSnipe` an Active arm (`snipeActive`)
that runs the §8.5 W/R pipeline — so a hit on the ACTIVE takes Weakness/Resistance while a
Benched one stays flat (the rules' "W/R apply only to the Active", conditional on the pick).
Lands Fezandipiti ex (100), Rotom (20), Paldean Tauros "Aqua Dive" (60), Bellibolt ex /
Kilowattrel (50). The put-counter snipe (Hawlucha / Meowscarada) and the benched-`deals`
families (Wo-Chien, riders) are UNCHANGED. The benched-snipe / any-target snipe family is now
broad; the remaining shapes are named below.
**Next concrete actions:**
1. **Chien-Pao ex "Hail Blade" — the last "×" sibling, a genuinely NEW shape (its own
   session).** "You may discard any amount of {W} Energy from your Pokémon. This attack does
   60 damage for each card you discarded in this way." A COMPOUND needing pieces the engine
   lacks: (a) a "discard ANY amount" `discardEnergy` mode from YOUR whole board (a new count
   mode + a multi-source pick), (b) a §9.2 record of the discarded count, and (c) the damage
   scaling by that recorded count. HARDEST: the discard is a PRE-damage park (choose how much
   BEFORE damage is calculated), which INVERTS the current damage-then-effect order. MED+/HARD.
2. **The remaining snipe RIDER/target shapes (all cheap now the op is proven):** the "also
   does N to EACH of your opponent's Benched" SPREAD rider (a `spreadDamage` rider — Cetoddle,
   1 card), the "also does N to 2 of …" COUNT-2 rider (`damageChosen count:2`), and a
   `perTakenPrize`+`opponentAny` combination if any card prints it. Umbreon "Feint Attack" is
   an `opponentAny` snipe whose damage "isn't affected by Weakness or Resistance" — a
   NO-W/R-even-on-the-Active flag (a small `damageChosen` option). LOW/MED.
3. **The last cheap reader of the D40 vocabulary: Defiance Band** — a conditional PASSIVE;
   `passivesOf` (continuous.ts) takes NO seat today and `PassiveEffects` has no conditional
   shape, so it needs a seat (or a `BoardCondition` evaluator) threaded through `passivesOf`
   + its two attack.ts call sites. MED.
4. Or pivot to **P4 (online matches)** — the engine is broad enough for real games.
**Recorded, NOT fixed (this slice):** `snipeActive` DUPLICATES attack.ts's §8.5 W/R pipeline
(base → ×Weakness → −Resistance → −reduction) rather than sharing a helper — a small, faithful
copy (a snipe omits the continuous pre-W/R bonus, which belongs to the main hit), acceptable
until a third consumer justifies extraction. `snipeActive`'s reduction term + the pre-W/R-bonus
omission are not INDEPENDENTLY pinned (no in-tree fixture gives an Active both a reduction
passive AND is sniped) — analysis-only, matching the benched arm's own reduction test.
**Carried forward (pre-existing, NOT this slice):** `legal_standard = 0` on most Trainers in
the local ingest; `GamePage`'s `passDisabled` phase check is untested; `validateChoice` does
not pin a multi-count pick to a single host; `handCostUnmet` is not compositional across two
costs in one program; the played Trainer sits UNDER its own payment in the discard pile; no
test anywhere covers an onEvolve trigger firing through Rare Candy; `maxPerTarget > 1` has no
printed consumer; a full target row's disabled STYLING is unpinned (house style); the
returned-Pokémon doctrine gap stays LATENT (§9.3); and `healUpToNote`'s `"all"` arm is still
dead code awaiting a printed author.

checked against the same starting hand, so a hand that can pay one would pass and

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 attack programs can PARK, kept for continuity)
**Attack effect programs can PARK (P3-M5, D42) — the `attackEpilogue` stage.** The
top backlog row is done, and it is a MECHANISM, not a card family: every future
attack effect may now hold a decision. `attack.ts` used to run an attack's effect
program as `runProgram(...).state`, so a parked result dropped the prompt AND the
remaining ops. Now the tail is **queued before the program runs** — a new
`PendingStage` **`{kind:"attackEpilogue", seat, koedSeat}`** carrying the §8.1 KO
sweep + the §5.3 turn end — and the fold goes through `settleProgram`'s
**`resumeTail`**. `finishAttack` moved into flow.ts (exported) because `advance` must
reach it and attack.ts already imports flow.
**`resumeTail` now means "mid-TAIL", not "mid-KO-sweep"** — the stages that finish
the job are queued behind the park, so DONE means keep draining. Its two producers
differ only for the projection: an on-KO park's `phase.seat` is NOT the turn owner,
an attack park's IS, and `koParkActiveSeat` resolves both off the pending queue
(`attackEpilogue` joined `endTurn`/`checkup`/`resumeTurn` as an in-turn marker).
**The first family is DERIVED, so it costs no registry rows:** `discardEnergy`
gained **`from: "yourActive"`** (the controller's own Active — for an attack, the
printed "this Pokémon", §8) and **`count: "all"`**, and two anchored whole-sentence

Staraptor, Paldean Tauros, Dedenne ex (×2), Bombirdier; Pawmot (×2), Raichu (×2).

identity) — a Houndoom attacking with three {R} asks nothing (the M1 no-choice
doctrine applied to card identity, via `attachEnergyFrom`'s fungibility precedent).
A **Basic** Energy's identity is what it PROVIDES, not its catalog id: the real
catalog prints Basic Fire Energy under sve-002/010/018, and an id key would park a
real deck on a non-choice. This also CHANGED D41's hammer arms (two copies of one

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 discardEnergy, kept for continuity)
**`discardEnergy` is live (P3-M5, D41) — the energy-removal "hammer" family.** ONE op
takes Energy off the **OPPONENT's** in-play Pokémon, and **`from` names both the
eligible Pokémon and how many are hit**, spelled the way the cards are:
**`opponentActive`** (Mawile), **`opponentChosen`** (Crushing Hammer — "from 1 of your
opponent's Pokémon"), **`opponentEach`** (Giacomo — "from each of…", skipping any
Pokémon with no match, the "do as much as you can" rule). All three arms land with a
REAL printed card, so nothing in the vocabulary is speculative.
**Exactly one Energy per affected Pokémon — no `count` field**, because every printed
"discard 2 / discard all" variant is an ATTACK, and attacks cannot park (see below).
**`opponentChosen` is a ONE-step decision, not two:** since exactly one Energy comes
off, picking the Energy IS picking the Pokémon — so the prompt is a flat candidate list
with none of the source/destination coupling that made `moveEnergy` (D37) compound.
**The engine's FIRST mandatory park:** every prior parking op was "up to" (searchDeck /
discardPileRetrieval / lookAtTopN / moveEnergy) or exactly-one (choosePokemon); here the
only question is WHICH Energy, never whether, so `validateChoice` enforces an EXACT
count and an empty pick is an ERROR, not a decline. The two scopes fall out of two rules
plus a count (every uid offered and distinct, no Pokémon gives up two, total = 1 or the
number of distinct sources — "one each, none skipped" then follows by pigeonhole). New
**`specialEnergy`** CardFilter; one **`ENERGY_DISCARDED`** event per affected Pokémon
(`seat` names the VICTIM, the DAMAGE_DEALT convention); the card goes to its **OWNER's**
discard pile. Never damages, so it never KOs. engineVersion 0.20.0 → **0.21.0**.
**Web: one dialog, one log row, NO projection change** — every candidate is Energy
sitting face up on the table. `DiscardEnergyDialog` groups candidates by host, has no
decline button (mandatory), **pre-answers forced groups** (a single-candidate group is
not a question), and carries the SPOT in the group legend ("· Bench 1") because two
copies of one Basic would otherwise give identical legends over identical rows.
**Review (adversarial engine+rules + web+integration): no HIGH in the slice's own logic
from either — but the engine review REVERSED a documented decision of mine.** I had
shipped Crushing Hammer as playable into an Energy-LESS board, reasoning that
`programPlayable` scans top-level ops only and "the flip happens either way". That is
**wrong**: §7 "you cannot play a card if it has no valid target" (Compendium
[ruling/906](https://compendium.pokegym.net/ruling/906/), reconfirmed by the TPCi Rules
Team **2025-06-26**) covers it, because **a coin flip is PROCEDURE, not effect**. The
apparent counter-precedent (Unown-E's Hidden Power forcing all flips tails, yet flip
Trainers staying playable) is the OTHER branch of
[ruling/284](https://compendium.pokegym.net/ruling/284/): blocked by an EFFECT in play →
playable; blocked by the **game state** → not. So **`programPlayable` now DESCENDS into
`coinFlipGate.then`**, which also fixes a **PRE-EXISTING** bug the slice merely
inherited — **Pokémon Catcher** was likewise playable into an empty opponent Bench.
**Poké Ball is deliberately untouched** (a deck is not public knowledge, so "this search
will find nothing" is never a fact the state establishes — the ruling's own limit), and
the check is **not** extended to `conditionGate` (no printed card needs it, and doing it
properly means evaluating the condition and scanning only the arm that runs).
The engine agent's **45-mutant** run left 5 real survivors, ALL test-adequacy, all now
dead — notably `refKeyOf` dropping the bench index (two benched holders would FUSE into
one group and park instead of auto-resolving) and `!==` → `<` on the required count (in
scope "one" that would accept two Energy off two DIFFERENT Pokémon; only the exact count
catches it). The web agent's 3 MEDs are all fixed (log-row tone, `fieldset`/`legend`
grouping, six missing tests).

declined, because `discardEnergy` is the first MANDATORY parking op — every earlier
auto-fired optional trigger escaped through its own declinable op. Left as-is and
pinned: the auto-fire doctrine's justification is that such triggers are PURE UPSIDE,
and this one is (no sv01–03 Special Energy's loss helps its owner), so it costs a click;
the real fix is the trigger-level yes/no confirm the doctrine already contemplates.
**P4 item surfaced (pre-existing):** `projection.ts` returns `pendingDecision` for BOTH
viewers ungated on `phase.seat` — harmless here, but the sibling `chooseCards` prompt
built by `searchDeck` carries the controller's DECK uids.

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 board conditions, kept for continuity)
**Board conditions are live (P3-M5, D40) — one `BoardCondition` vocabulary, TWO
consumers.** The `conditionalPlay` family, built as a primitive instead of a per-card
flag. **`BoardCondition`** (effects.ts) is a predicate union evaluated for ONE seat —
**`morePrizesThanOpponent`** (strict `>`: you are BEHIND on Prizes taken),
**`yourStadiumInPlay`**, **`noEnergyOnYourPokemon`** (Active AND Bench, Basic or
Special) — behind a single evaluator **`conditionHolds`** and a printed-text describer
**`conditionNote`**. **The invariant IS the design: every member reads only PUBLIC
state**, which is exactly why **a gate emits no event** — contrast `coinFlipGate`,
whose flip is genuinely new information; a board condition is a fact both players can
read off the table, and the branch's own ops emit whatever happened.
**Consumer A — the printed PLAY GATE:** `CardProgram.trainerPlayableIf`, checked by
`playTrainer` BEFORE the card leaves hand (new `ErrorCode` `PLAY_CONDITION_NOT_MET`),
so a failed gate costs nothing. Categorically different from `programPlayable`'s
would-only-whiff heuristics: this is a rule PRINTED on the card. Named `trainer…`
because it is honoured on EXACTLY one path — `playStadium`/`rareCandy`/`attachTool`/
`useAbility` all return before it and would ignore it SILENTLY (the `trainerEndsTurn`
precedent; it is also why Luxray's Ability gate must NOT be authored here).
**Consumer B — the mid-program branch:** the **`conditionGate`** op
`{cond, then, otherwise?}`, spliced into runProgram's work queue exactly like
`coinFlipGate` (an op inside a branch can still park, and a branch may hold further
gates), evaluated against the board AS OF the gate. One-armed is the common shape
(Falkner); `otherwise` is the printed "…**instead**", a real if/ELSE (Grusha).
**One tiny new automatic op — `drawUntilHandSize`:** it DRAWS to a floor and never

cards" row). Lands **3 COMPLETE real cards** (verified vs local D1): **Fighting Au
Lait** (sv02-181 — the gate + heal 60), **Falkner** (sv02-180/251 — two draw ops, not
one computed count, so the log shows both printed instructions), **Grusha**
(sv02-184/253/268 — the `otherwise` arm; its hand count is measured AFTER the Supporter
is discarded up front, the paper ruling for the hand-size family).
**Web: zero new events, prompts, dialogs or projection fields.** The one change is the
HUD greying a gated Trainer out with the engine's own `conditionHolds`, carrying
`conditionNote` as the row's `title` + an `sr-only` line — load-bearing copy, because
disabling the button REMOVES the reject pill that used to explain the printed rule.
engineVersion 0.19.0 → **0.20.0**.
**Review (adversarial engine+rules + web+integration): NO HIGH from either.** The
engine agent verified the slice's riskiest claim — **`yourStadiumInPlay` is OWNERSHIP,
not presence** — against the Japanese printing of ハヤト
(「場に**自分の**スタジアムが出ているなら」) and Bulbapedia; an opponent's Stadium must
not grant Falkner's +2. Its 24-mutant run left 5 survivors (1 equivalent), ALL
test-adequacy, all now fixed and re-verified dead with two new fixtures:

and an op AFTER the gate — one ordered `CARDS_DRAWN` assertion kills the
evaluate-against-entry-state, push-not-unshift and dropped-tail mutants at once) and
**fix-gatedsup** (the only gated SUPPORTER, pinning that a rejected gate does not burn
the §7.2 allowance). The web agent's 4 MEDs are all addressed: the missing
`engineVersion` bump; unpinned log rows (3 tests, incl. Falkner's PAIR of draw rows and
Grusha's zero-row case); a **self-defeating** doc claim that "a P4 client may evaluate
one locally"; and the HUD's opponent-`prizes` read.

gate while `programPlayable`'s whiff gates (Boss's Orders into an empty Bench) stay

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 Iono, kept for continuity)
**Iono is live (P3-M5, D39) — the hand-refresh Supporter family is CLOSED.** The
format's highest-play-rate Supporter needed **no new op**: three composable riders on
the D38 `handRefresh` op. **`toBottom?: true`** — the PLACEMENT: shuffle the **hand
alone** and append it UNDER the deck (`[...deck, ...shuffle(hand)]`) instead of
shuffling it into the deck, so the deck's existing order — and therefore the very next
draws — SURVIVE (the whole strategic point of Iono over Judge; pinned by a test
asserting the drawn cards are EXACTLY the pre-play deck top, in order).
**`draw:{kind:"prizeCount"}`** — each affected player draws their OWN remaining Prize
count (the player behind draws more); a Prize count is public, so the draw size leaks
nothing. **`onlyIfAnyMoved?: true`** — the draw clause fires only if ≥1 affected player
actually moved ≥1 card: an **all-or-nothing gate ACROSS the seats** ("if EITHER
player…"), not per-seat. That gate forced the op's one structural change: **two passes**
over the affected seats (all placements, then all draws) instead of D38's interleaved
move-then-draw — **behaviour-preserving** for Youngster/Judge/Brassius/Katy (per-seat
disjoint zones + `drawToHand` consumes NO rng ⇒ byte-identical states and rng threading,
verified by reconstructing the old loop and diffing at 3 seeds each); the only change is
Judge's event INTERLEAVING (SHUFFLED p1, SHUFFLED p2, DRAWN p1, DRAWN p2 — which also
reads truer to the printed sentence). `shuffle` consumes nothing for a length ≤ 1 input,
so an Iono into two empty hands advances the rng ZERO times. One new count-only event
**`HAND_TO_BOTTOM_OF_DECK {seat, count}`** — distinct from its sibling because the public
fact differs (the deck's order is untouched, which both players must be able to read off
the log). **Web: one log row, no dialog** (never parks, no projection change) — "shuffled
their hand (N cards) and put it on the bottom of their deck": it must say BOTH verbs,
since the hand IS randomized on its way under an unshuffled deck. Lands **Iono**
(sv02-185/254/269, verified vs local D1). engine 0.18.0 → **0.19.0**.
**Review (adversarial engine+rules + web+integration): no HIGH; 2 MED, both FIXED.** The
engine MED was found by **mutation testing** — deleting the hand shuffle left all 379
engine tests green (every bottom assertion was order-insensitive; nothing asserted
`rngState`) → added `.not.toEqual(handOrder)` + `rngState` assertions on both the
shuffled and the zero-randomness paths; the mutant now dies. The web MED (raised
independently by BOTH agents) was the log copy implying Iono does NOT shuffle → fixed.
LOWs applied: an Iono degenerate-deck test (deck shallower than the Prize count
short-draws, no deck-out), a describe rename, and a real end-to-end log test pinning the
grouped 5-row batch. **Deliberate deviation (recorded in D39, not accidental):** Iono
with EVERY affected hand empty is a total no-op yet stays LEGAL (no `programPlayable`
gate, unlike gust/switch/attach/moveEnergy) — the digital clients allow it, it cannot
soft-lock, and a gate would have to reach into "playTrainer discards the played card up
front" (the D35 leaky coupling). **The family is CLOSED** — no Marnie in the sv01–03
catalog. See "M5 op-slice: handRefresh riders as built" + D39.
**Next concrete actions (keep building the backlog):**
1. **The `conditionalPlay` / board-condition gate family** (5 backlog cards) — and the
   same primitive also unlocks **Falkner** ("if you have a Stadium in play, draw 2
   more") and, with a `drawUntilHandSize` op, **Grusha**. The biggest remaining cluster.
2. **The remaining `moveEnergy` cards** each layer a rider: **Armarouge** "Fire Off" (a
   {R} Energy benched→Active — fixed-endpoint + provided-type filter, an Ability),
   **Mismagius** "Magical Flick" (the OPPONENT's Energy on evolve — opponent-side +
   onEvolve trigger), **Exp. Share** (an on-KO Tool trigger).
3. **The from-the-top attach variant** (Electric Generator / Hydreigon) — also closes 2
   of the remaining `attachEnergyFrom` cards — or **`discardOpponentEnergy`** (Crushing
   Hammer / Giacomo, 4). See `docs/reference/coverage-backlog.md`.
4. **Miriam** is the near-miss worth naming: its "if you shuffled any cards in this way,
   draw 3" is `onlyIfAnyMoved`'s idea but BETWEEN ops and across a park — it needs an
   op-result threaded through the interpreter's continuation, not a flag. Deferred.
5. Or pivot to **P4 (online matches)** — the engine is broad enough to play real games;
   the projection is already P4's per-viewer filter, and the standing deck-candidate
   INFO (searchDeck/lookAtTopN `pendingDecision.prompt`) is exactly what its server-side
   redaction must cover. Iono, like the rest of handRefresh, needs none of it.
**Two pre-existing items the review surfaced (NOT this slice):** every authored
Supporter has `legal_standard=0` in the local ingest, so none surface in the builder's
default standard-legal search; and `GameLog` announces only the last entry to screen
readers, so a 5-row batch is mostly silent (P5 polish).

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 handRefresh, kept for continuity)
**`handRefresh` is live (P3-M5, D38) — shuffle your hand into your deck, then draw.**
The Iono/Judge/Marnie hand-refresh Supporter family. New op `{who:"you"|"both", draw}`
— the FIRST op in a new class: **fully AUTOMATIC** (no decision → it NEVER parks, like
drawCards/discardHand/shuffleDeck) AND it can affect the **opponent** (`who:"both"`,
Judge — the first op to reach the OPPONENT's hand/deck). Per affected seat (controller
first, then — for `both` — the opponent) it captures the PRE-shuffle hand size, moves
the whole hand into the deck, shuffles the combined pile (`shuffle([...deck, ...hand])`
— one rng advance, threaded fresh each iteration so the two-shuffle Judge has no stale
reuse), then draws per **`HandRefreshDraw`**: `{fixed count}` (Youngster 5, Judge 4,
Katy 8) or `{handPlus delta}` (Brassius "draw that many cards plus 1"). **Card
conservation** is a pure multiset move (`[...deck, ...hand]` → shuffle → draw back),
invariant under empty-hand / empty-deck / hand==whole-deck / both-empty; the Supporter
is discarded UP FRONT, so never shuffled back. **Always playable** (no `programPlayable`
gate); never damages/KOs. **Katy "your turn ends"** lands the `endsTurn` fold on the
TRAINER path — a new CardProgram flag **`trainerEndsTurn`** that `playTrainer` passes
to `settleProgram`, folded byte-for-byte like Koraidon's `AbilityProgram.endsTurn`
(D34); every non-Katy trainer passes `endsTurn:false` (byte-identical, no regression).
One new count-only event **`HAND_SHUFFLED_INTO_DECK {seat, count}`** (the deck reorder
is intrinsic — no separate `SHUFFLE`). Lands **4 COMPLETE real Supporters** (verified
vs local D1): **Youngster** (sv01-198, draw 5), **Judge** (sv01-176, both draw 4),
**Brassius** (sv03-187, draw hand+1), **Katy** (sv01-177/237, draw 8 + turn ends).
**Web: one log row, no dialog** — handRefresh never parks, so no new `EffectPrompt`/
dialog (GameHud untouched); one count-only `HAND_SHUFFLED_INTO_DECK` row, the draw
riding the existing count-only `CARDS_DRAWN`. **Hidden info (Judge — the first op to
touch the opponent's hand): leaks NOTHING new** — the opponent's `CARDS_DRAWN` uids are
the standard `drawToHand` contract; the log arms are count-only and the projection
already redacts the opponent's hand to uid-less backs. engine 0.17.0 → **0.18.0**.
**Adversarial review (engine+rules + web+integration): BOTH CLEAN — no HIGH/MED, NO
code fixes** (card conservation over all four degenerate zone states, two-shuffle rng
threading, handPlus timing, the Katy endsTurn fold with no regression across the full
374-test engine suite, purity against a recursive freeze, all four texts byte-matching
the catalog / no missed reprint, Judge hidden-info safe on both log + projection). INFO
(both, not bugs): an empty hand emits `count:0` (honest, non-leaky — the `HAND_DISCARDED
"(0 cards)"` precedent); the no-separate-`SHUFFLE`-event choice is cosmetic with no
consumer. Closes the `shuffleHandIntoDeck` + `endTurn` backlog rows. See "M5 op-slice:
handRefresh as built" + D38.
**Next concrete actions (keep building the backlog):**
1. **Iono / Marnie** layer on this primitive: they put the hand on the BOTTOM of the
   deck (not shuffle) and draw by Prize count (Iono) / an asymmetric split (Marnie —
   you 5, opponent 4) — a bottom-of-deck move + a `prizeCount`/split `HandRefreshDraw`.
   High play rate; small additions on `handRefresh`.
2. **The remaining `moveEnergy` cards** each layer a rider: **Armarouge** "Fire Off" (a
   {R} Energy benched→Active — fixed-endpoint + provided-type filter, an Ability),
   **Mismagius** "Magical Flick" (the OPPONENT's Energy on evolve — opponent-side +
   onEvolve trigger), **Exp. Share** (an on-KO Tool trigger).
3. **The next backlog op by unlock count** — the **`conditionalPlay`** family (5, a
   "you can use this only if <board condition>" gate — but each card still needs its
   effect op too), a **from-the-top attach** variant (Electric Generator / Hydreigon,
   also 2 `attachEnergyFrom` cards), or **`discardOpponentEnergy`** (Crushing Hammer /
   Giacomo, 4). See `docs/reference/coverage-backlog.md`.
4. Or pivot to **P4 (online matches)** — the engine is broad enough to play real games;
   the projection is already P4's per-viewer filter, and the deck-candidate INFO
   (searchDeck/lookAtTopN) is exactly what its server-side redaction must cover
   (`pendingDecision.prompt`) — `handRefresh`'s all-count-only events need none.

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 moveEnergy, kept for continuity)
**`moveEnergy` is live (P3-M5, D37) — move Energy between your own Pokémon.** A new
op `{filter, max}` moves up to `max` Energy from ONE of the controller's own in-play
Pokémon to ANOTHER — the interpreter's **first op with two COUPLED decisions** (which
Energy AND where). Unlike every prior op (which reused one existing prompt), it adds a
**new compound prompt** `moveEnergy` (`movable`: each takeable Energy uid tagged with
its source `PokemonRef`; `destinations`: all own in-play refs) and a **new choice**
`{uids, dest}` answering both at once, applied **ATOMICALLY** by `moveEnergyApply`
(strip the picks off their source, append to the dest in one `withSide` — a floating
detached-Energy state never exists, which is why it is one compound park not two).
"Up to"/declinable; always parks when playable. **`validateChoice`** enforces the
couplings (each uid an offered `movable`, distinct, ALL sharing ONE source, dest
offered, **dest ≠ source**), so no illegal wire move applies; `moveEnergyApply`
conserves cards and is pure. New **`programPlayable` gate** (`moveEnergyPlayable`: ≥1
matching Energy AND ≥2 of your Pokémon in play) = the exact complement of stepOp's
no-op (no wasted card, no soft-lock). One new `CardFilter` **`anyEnergy`** (Basic OR
Special) + one new event `ENERGY_MOVED {seat, uids, from, to}`. Lands **Energy
Switch** (sv01-173) and **Poppy** (sv03-193/220/227) — 2 of the op's 5 backlog cards.
**Web:** `MoveEnergyDialog` (a staged pick, or **Move none**) + one `ENERGY_MOVED` log
row; the prompt leaks NOTHING (own face-up in-play Energy/Pokémon). engine 0.16.0 →
**0.17.0**. Review (adversarial engine+rules + web + an independent Opus pass): CLEAN —
no HIGH/MED; one action (a two-source Poppy DOM test). See "M5 op-slice: moveEnergy as
built" + D37.

opponent's turn — the inverse of the slice-8 snipe (the KO fires the trigger).
`TriggerTiming` += **`"onKnockOut"`**; detection is triggers.ts
**`onKnockOutTrigger`** (via `cardIdByUid → programFor`, valid after the KO
discarded the card), but flow.ts's KO sweep DRIVES it. Two forms on
`TriggeredAbility`: (1) a coin-flip **Prize GUARD** (`onKoPrizeGuard:
"coinFlipPrevent"` — Glimmora: heads → the opponent takes no Prize for it),
resolved INLINE by a new **`planPrizes`** (flow.ts) run UP FRONT — before the §14
tie-guard speculation — threading rng ONCE so the speculation and the real KO
share the post-flip count (§14 stays exact), the guard's events firing after the
`KNOCKED_OUT`; and (2) a general parking **PROGRAM** run as a new **`koTrigger`
PendingStage** (`advance` → **`runKoTrigger`** → **`settleProgram` with a new
`resumeTail`** flag): it PARKS on `effect:choose` (where `phase.seat` is the KO'd,
NON-turn player) and, on `resolveEffect`, the sweep RESUMES draining the queued
prize/promotion tail instead of folding back to a turn. Batch order:
PRIZES-first, then koTriggers, then promotions; a §14 game-ending prize skips the
program, while the guard (resolved earlier) can DENY a winning prize.
Behaviour-neutral for every card with no on-KO Ability. Representatives Glimmora

### 2026-09-07 — build session #421 (P3-M5 — D481)

**THE TYPECHECK HOLE OVER `scripts/` — CLOSED, and the count refutes the forecast that justified
taking it.** Engine **0.377.0 UNCHANGED**, `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **29**, mutation corpus
**2,238 → 2,246**, archive ratchet **150 → 151**, `bun run check` GREEN at **468 files / 10,568
tests**.

**(0) 🛑 THE MEASUREMENT, TAKEN BEFORE ANY CONFIG CHANGED: SIX ERRORS IN TWO FILES.** Two are
**environmental, not defects** — `bun:sqlite` and the `Bun` global, with no types package installed.
**Four are real and all in ONE instrument** (`residue-census.ts`): two `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`
tuple-index errors and two failures to narrow a `string | null`. **And the single most important
number is a ZERO: `mutants.ts` — 2.30 MiB, 2,238 rows — had NO errors.** The corpus is annotated
`export const MUTANTS: Mutant[]`, so **excess-property checking was always latent there and nothing
was running it**; D480's `survives.why` was the one instance and D480 had already fixed it.

**(1) 🛑 THE HOLE WAS 15 FILES, NOT 12 — AND THE THREE EXTRA ARE THE POINT.** `apps/api/drizzle.config.ts`,
`apps/api/scripts/ingest.ts` and `packages/schema/scripts/validate-live.ts` live **outside
`scripts/`**, and **no document names them** — this brief, D480's decisions row and the resume point
all called it a `scripts/` hole. ⚠️ **Framing a coverage gap by the directory where it was noticed
would have left three files behind a guard that then reported OK** — which is the same defect one
level up. The fix covers the whole dev-tooling region, not the directory the witness happened to
live in.

**(2) THE FORECAST THAT JUSTIFIED THE SLICE WAS FALSE, AND SAYING SO IS PART OF THE RESULT.**
`conventions.md`'s *"expect it to surface latent errors in proportion to how long it was open"* did
**not** hold: six errors, four in one file, zero in the corpus and zero in four of the five
instruments. ⚠️ **The ECONOMICS half of that entry was right — a defect there cost a 2.7-hour sweep
to find — and the VOLUME half was wrong.** A long-open hole is expensive per defect, not necessarily
rich in them; the two are independent, and only the first is an argument for closing it.

**(3) THE PROOF THE CLOSE IS REAL RATHER THAN NOMINAL.** D480's exact witness, re-run as a mutant —
`reason:` → `why:` in the corpus — **now dies to `bun run typecheck` with TS2353 in 38.2 seconds**,
where the only instrument that could previously see it was a ~2.7-hour whole-corpus sweep. That row
is now in the corpus and **is the only one whose killer is the typechecker**; it could not have
existed one commit earlier.

**(4) THE GUARD IS D212's TWIN, 269 DECISIONS LATE, AND IT ASSERTS THREE THINGS PROSE CANNOT.**
`scripts/typecheck-coverage.ts` asks each project `tsc -p <p> --showConfig` and reads the
**compiler's own expanded file list** rather than re-implementing glob semantics. It **holds no
number of its own** (D465) — files from `git`, projects from `tsconfig.json`, lists from `tsc`. It
has **no exemption list, asserted rather than merely absent.** And it **asserts its own wiring**:
`lint-coverage.ts` can be disabled by deleting eight words from `package.json` with nothing going
red, so this one reads `scripts.check` and requires its own path in it.

**(5) THE SELF-CHECK IS WHAT MAKES A MUTANT ROW AGAINST IT A ROW.** A coverage guard's one
unkillable failure mode is going **vacuous** — blank the predicate or widen `=== 0` to `<= 1` and it
passes forever, and a sweep mutating it reports SURVIVED and is believed (D479's class, at the
address where it is hardest to notice). So the verdict routes through two drivable functions
exercised on **synthetic pairs whose answer is known by construction**, before the repo is consulted
at all. ⚠️ **That is the board on which the guard's own absence is observable** — without it, the
guard would have been exactly the defect this slice exists to fix.

**(6) A RUNG WAS WRITTEN AND DELETED AS UNREACHABLE, WHICH IS THE RIGHT OUTCOME.** A
"this project contributes zero files" check could never fire: `tsc -p … --showConfig` exits 1 with
**TS18003** first. **The vacuous-config case is caught — by the compiler, one call earlier.** A rung
that cannot fire is not a weaker guard, it is not a guard (D475's rule, applied to a rung rather
than a mutant row). Deletion documented in place.

**(7) THE COST, MEASURED — AND THE BRIEF'S SUSPECT WAS INNOCENT.** `+3.2s` on `tsc -b` (+9.4%) and
`+0.78s` for the guard = **+4.0s on a ~171s gate, +2.3%**. ⚠️ **`mutants.ts` typechecks in 0.99s
including startup** — the 2.3 MB literal the brief suspected is not the cost driver; re-typechecking
engine and schema **sources** is, because the instruments import them by relative path. And a
reference cannot serve that: `packages/engine` is `noEmit` by design, so **the brief's question had
the opposite answer to the one it implied** — a project reference is not unnecessary here, it is
*unavailable* without turning the engine into an emitting project for a dev tool's sake.

**(8) TWO GUARD MUTATIONS DECLARED NOT ROWS, AND NAMED AS THE RESIDUAL RISK.** Dropping `"tsx"` from
the extension list, and dropping `--others` from `git ls-files`, both **narrow the guard's
population silently**, are green on a clean tree, and **nothing can kill either**. Declared rather
than shipped weak (D475/D479). ⚠️ **Two one-token edits can shrink what the guard audits without
going red, and naming them is the only mitigation available** — the predicate is over ROOT files,
not PROGRAM files, and the guard says nothing about compiler OPTIONS.

**(9) `@types/bun` DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED.** A 50-line shim declares only the two Bun signatures
`scripts/` actually reaches. **Price stated rather than hidden: those signatures are unverified
claims** — if Bun's API differs, one script typechecks against a fiction. Mitigated by narrowness,
not solved: a *new* Bun API fails with "property does not exist" rather than silently becoming
`any`. Refused because a slice about verification coverage should not also be the slice that adds a
dependency tree whose global redeclarations were not measured.

  at all had to be this loose: the sentences print no count, no verb the family does not
  share and no noun of their own, so the only token unique to them is the unit.

  sibling in this family reads a printed COUNT and × 10s it at the producer (§12); these
  print a DESTINATION. The amount is `effectiveMaxHp − damage − remainingHp`, evaluated
  **inside the per-body closure** — which IS the printed distributive *"its"*, so the op
  carries no `amount` field at all and the naive one-figure build is unconstructible
  rather than merely wrong. The field it does carry is **HP and not counters**, so the two
  arms do NO conversion: the one line they could have copied from a sibling and been wrong.

  HP is `effectiveMaxHp − damage`* is written at three shipped sites (`remainingHpWithin`'s
  doc block, `registry.ts`'s `KO_SURVIVAL` note, index.ts's D349 paragraph) and is what
  `remainingHpWithin` computes for the catalog's other three *"remaining HP"* printings. A
  Bravery Charm (+50) on a 200 HP body raises the destination it is filled to — 200 HP of
  counters, not 150 — and the printed reading would leave it at 100 remaining instead of
  50. A `null` maximum places NOTHING, `remainingHpWithin`'s refuse direction verbatim.

  both guard a CONSTANT handed in by the producer. This amount varies per body, so the
  guard must too: `healEach`/`healEachAll` have skipped per body on a computed `<= 0`
  since 0.x and are this op's exact mirror (they clamp to `damage`, it clamps to
  `max − damage − target`). A whole-op guard would let ONE body already under the
  destination cancel the fold for every other body, and that board is driven.
- 🛑 **(Q3) IT CANNOT KNOCK ANYTHING OUT, AND THE GUARANTEE IS ARITHMETIC.** A filled body
  lands at `damage = max − remainingHp`, lethal exactly when `remainingHp <= 0`. Pinned as
  a TOTAL check over maxima, destinations and starting damages — not as an observation
  about three printed rows — and made a property of the FUNCTION by an explicit
  `op.remainingHp <= 0` refusal, D324's move: the alternative is an invariant stated in

### 2026-08-24 — build session #351 (P3-M5 — D411, the journal liveness gate)

**D411 — THE SLICE THAT NAMES THE WRITER D410's SWEEP COULD NOT, BECAUSE IT WAS THIS SESSION'S OWN
RECOVERY COMMAND.** No engine change: **engine STAYS 0.315.0**, **`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` STAYS 25**,

🛑 **THE DEFECT: `recoverFromJournal()` WAS ASKED TWO QUESTIONS AND ANSWERED ONE.** *Is there a
journal* and *did the run that wrote it die* are different propositions — the journal is written
BEFORE every file change and cleared only at restore, so it is present for the **whole of a healthy
run**. Recovery is a WRITE, so running it against a live run's journal restores that run's mutant out
from under it, **deletes the journal that was its last `kill -9` net**, and leaves the in-flight row
reporting `CLOBBER` against a phantom "another process".

🛑 **AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT PRODUCED D410's ONE CLOBBER.** The sweep launched at 11:13 and ran 89
minutes; at 12:26 this session found a mutated `interpreter.ts` and a journal, read both as wreckage
from D410's dead agent, and ran `bun run mutants` to recover — **following this file's own documented
advice**. `D376-discard-threshold-note-drifts-off-the-clause` was mid-window. D410's row records the
writer as UNKNOWN and was right to refuse to guess; it was also right to exonerate `--list`
(measured: `sha256sum` unchanged, no journal created — D369's ordering fix holds). **The suspect was
one command over.**

⚠️ **D369 FOUND THIS CLASS AND FIXED THE INSTANCE.** Its repair moved `--list` ahead of the recovery
— correct, and about the one command that had no business writing at all — while every WRITING
invocation walked straight in for forty decisions. **A FIX THAT REORDERS ONE CALLER PAST A LANDMINE
LEAVES THE LANDMINE.**

✅ **THE SIGNATURE WAS PRESENT BOTH TIMES AND IS WORTH KEEPING**: the preserved "clobbered" file is
**byte-identical to `HEAD`**, which is the fingerprint of a RESTORE and not of an edit. D369 recorded
it; D410 measured it and did not recognise it; it is what made the cause findable in ten minutes here.

**THE FIX.** `pidIsAlive()` asks `process.kill(pid, 0)` — no signal, only addressability — and
recovery REFUSES on a live pid, writing nothing and exiting **3**, kept distinct from the **2** that
means *a dead run's files were put back, go look at the tree*. Collapsing the two would send an
automated caller to inspect a diff that does not exist. ⚠️ **PIDS ARE REUSED AND THE FAILURE
DIRECTION IS CHOSEN, NOT OVERLOOKED**: a recycled pid reads as alive and recovery refuses instead of
restoring — cost, one `rm` the message names by path; the opposite error is the defect itself.
`startedAt` is not a tie-break, because it is the JOURNAL's clock and not the process's.

🛑 **THE GUARD IS A PAIR, AND THE SECOND HALF IS WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS.**
`scripts/mutation/recovery-gate.ts` (D212's `killedByCommand` precedent — **only the second row in
the corpus to use it**) drives the real CLI twice with the SAME journal, differing only in whether
the pid is alive: one must refuse and leave every byte alone, the other must restore and clear.
**A GUARD ASSERTING ONLY THE REFUSAL IS ONE `return "in-flight"` AWAY FROM PASSING FOREVER WHILE
LAYER 4 STOPS WORKING ENTIRELY** — that is the C2 mutant, and the recover-half is the attribution
control (D214) that kills it.

a journal of its own in flight for the whole window, so `JOURNAL` is now overridable by
`MUTATION_JOURNAL_PATH` and the guard runs hermetically inside a temp dir — otherwise the guard for
the clobber defect would have committed it. Its blast radius is one file outside the repo, so it is
also safe to run beside a live sweep.

🛑 **A MUTANT SURVIVED ITS FIRST PROBE, AND THAT BOUGHT THE THIRD RUNG.** `process.kill(pid, 0)`
throws for two OPPOSITE reasons — `ESRCH` (gone) and `EPERM` (alive, not yours) — and both halves

`b × 2 + s × 2` — so both readings return the same number and a Weakness rung would be an identity
dressed as a guard, the exact vacuous shape conventions.md is about. **RESISTANCE IS A SUBTRACTION
AND IS PAID ONCE PER HIT**, so it separates them. On `fix-psychic-resist-big` (200 HP, −30 Psychic,
in the pool since D139) two discards deal:

    ONE pass (this build)   : (50 + 120) − 30 = 140
    TWO passes (the refusal): (50 − 30) + (120 − 30) = 110
    base DROPPED            : 120 − 30 = 90
    base NOT suppressed     : (50 − 30) + (50 + 120 − 30) = 160

Four numbers on one board, and only the first is right. `damageReductionAfterWR` and the §8.1
survival clamp make the same argument twice over.

**THE OBSTACLE IS A SIGNATURE, NOT A SHAPE.** `deriveAttackEffect` takes only a STRING; the printed
base is a field on the attack and lives in `attack.ts`. A captured `more` on D402's anchor would
have produced an op whose `base` nothing could populate — D163's finding on the `SELF_COUNTER_SCALE`
/ `SELF_COUNTER_MULTIPLY` pair reproduced one count-source over, and the same reader-plus-exported-
assembler shape D316/D317/D318/D381 already have. The handoff predicted this seam and it held; what
it got wrong is named below.

⚠️ **THE `scaledBase` CLAIMANT WAS OWED FOR AN *ORDERING* REASON, NOT A NESTING ONE.** The handoff
named `programDamage` / `scaledBase` as the likelier of its two falsifiers and it half-held. Those
three siblings claim the base because their `damageDefender` is NESTED inside a gate that
`programDamage`'s top-level `some` deliberately does not walk. **THIS ONE'S HIT IS A BARE TOP-LEVEL
OP, EXACTLY LIKE HAIL BLADE'S** — and the term is still owed, because `programDamage` is computed
from the registry/derived program FOUR HUNDRED LINES ABOVE the append, so no reading-borne program
can ever reach it. **THE PREDICTION WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE TERM AND WRONG ABOUT WHY**, and the wrong
reason is precisely the one a future reader would have re-derived from `programDamage`'s own doc.

union's doc called its three own-board members *"a spot, a side and a body"*; this is a FOURTH kind

· **DELEGATE → MEMBER, and this is the clause that was let bind.** `yourBenchDamaged`'s arm is an

purpose (`onlyIf`/`barredIf`, `then`/`otherwise`), so a forgotten optional `name` is silently wrong
in opposite directions and is never a type error.

clause **2/4**, which is chance. **THE NOTE CLAUSE IS RETIRED AS A DECIDER** and kept as a COST
note; what remains is *a filter is a FIELD only when a SHIPPED delegate already accepts it;
otherwise a MEMBER — and if the value is read at two polarities, MEMBER regardless.*
**A RULE TESTED THREE TIMES AND AMENDED ONCE IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE ASSERTED FIVE TIMES.**

### 2026-08-22 — build session #334 (P3-M5 — D394, the used-attack pair: whose clock, and which comes first — the read or the write)

**D394 — THE UNION HALF WAS TRIVIAL AND THERE WERE TWO REAL QUESTIONS.** Falinks `sv07-088`
"All-Out Attack" ({C}{C}, `30+`, **+90**, index **1** of TWO) and Weezing `sv09-092` "Crazy Blast"
({D}{C}, `50+`, **+120**, index 1 of TWO), **1 legal printing each** — *"If this Pokémon used Form
Ranks during your last turn, this attack does 90 more damage."* and *"…used Pervasive Gas…, 120 more
damage."* Both located with ONE brace-free limitlesstcg `text:` search each on the printed clause
tail (`SCR 88`, `JTG 92`, one card each) and confirmed field by field against
`https://api.tcgdex.net/v2/en/cards/<id>`, **including the attack at index 0 that each clause NAMES**
— which is the half a card-name search does not give you. 🆕 **A CLAUSE THAT QUOTES AN ATTACK NAME
HAS A TAIL SEARCH JUST AS A CLAUSE THAT QUOTES A CARD NAME DOES**, and the run's set-code map is now
`SCR = sv07`, `SSP = sv08`, `JTG = sv09`, `DRI = sv10`.

**QUESTION ONE — WHOSE CLOCK, AND IT WAS MEASURED.** The handoff said `state.turn - 2` was a GUESS
that had to be driven across a KO park before the comparison was written, and it was right to. Both
park shapes were built:

  · **ATTACK-EPILOGUE PARK** — P1 declares at `turn = 3`; the KO parks in `ko:takePrizes` and then
    `ko:promote` **both at `turn = 3`**, with `pending` = `takePrizes, promote, endTurn, checkup,
    startTurn`; the board sits at 4 once the tail drains and P1's next turn is **5**. Δ = 2.
  · **CHECKUP PARK** — a lethal poison tick between turns parks at the ENDING turn's value with
    `pending` = `takePrizes, promote, startTurn`. Two consecutive parks: 1 → 3. Δ = 2.

The mechanism is that **`turnTail` queues exactly ONE `startTurn` and every KO stage is spliced in
FRONT of it**, so no park can insert or skip a counter step. `state.turn - 2` is therefore D143's
`state.turn + 2` reflected — the same claim (*"declaring an attack ends the turn, so the turn after
this one is the opponent's"*) read backwards. A `- 1` would have been the OPPONENT's clock and would
compare against a turn number no body of this seat can carry; mutant **C1** installs exactly that,
copied verbatim from `koedDuringOpponentsLastTurn` four lines up in the same file.

🆕 **AND THE PARITY DOES THE SEAT CHECK FOR FREE.** `state.turn - 2` shares the current turn's
parity, and a body is only ever stamped on turns its own controller held (the §8 gate refuses an
attack from the seat that does not hold `turn:action`). So the arm evaluated OFF-TURN for the
non-turn seat compares against a turn number that seat's bodies cannot carry and gets an honest
FALSE — `yourFirstTurn`'s guarantee arrived at a THIRD way, by arithmetic instead of by operand
choice, and with no `phaseViewOf` guard to forget.

**QUESTION TWO — WHICH COMES FIRST, THE READ OR THE WRITE, AND NO EARLIER STAMP HAD TO ASK IT.**
`promotedTurn`, `healedTurn` and `evolvedTurn` are all written by something that is not the attack,
so their read and their write could not collide. This one is written BY the attack and read BY the
attack. `scaledAttackDamage`'s `boardCondition` arm evaluates the clause **at declaration**
(attack.ts, D115's placement — whose own comment says it is there so *"Gyarados ex's 'already has any
damage counters on it' cannot be bootstrapped by this very attack"*), so a stamp written beside
`ATTACK_DECLARED` would overwrite LAST turn's record with THIS turn's attack **before that read**,
and the printed +90 and +120 would never pay on any board while every board still looked plausible.

**SO THE ONE WRITER IS `finishAttack` (flow.ts), AND THAT CHOICE IS ALSO AN ARGUMENT ABOUT WHAT
"USED" MEANS.** That function IS this engine's definition of it: attack.ts's four exits reach it (the
confusion-tails failure, the D125 requirement gate whose own comment already said *"a cancelled
attack is an attack that was USED"*, the cancel-on-tails flip and the no-program tail) plus the
parked program's epilogue stage, and the Checkup and mid-turn KO sweeps never do. ⚠️ **THE PARKED
ROUTE IS WHY `PendingStage.attackEpilogue` GAINED A REQUIRED `attack`** — it is the one of the five
on which `declared.name` is out of scope by the time the stamp is written, which is D189's argument
about `uid` with the subject changed from *which body* to *which attack*. Mutant **C6** drops it and
is invisible on the other four routes.

**THE SHAPE.** A MEMBER by D391's rule (a new board fact), and its payload field is **`attack` and
not `name`** because the member directly above it in the union carries a `name` that is a POKÉMON

free-retreat auras short-circuiting to 0. **They disagree on every board carrying a retreat Stadium or
a retreat aura, and this pool has four such levers.** So the question was never *"which do I build"*
but *"which does the sentence NAME"*, and D387 left the row unbuilt for exactly that reason.

**THE FOLD IS TAKEN, ON THREE GROUNDS AND NOT ON TASTE:**

⑴ 🛑 **THE ENGINE HAD ALREADY ANSWERED THIS EXACT NOUN PHRASE, AND D159 FORBIDS A SECOND ANSWER.**
`DamageCountSource`'s `opponentActiveRetreatCost` (D110) reads *"for each {C} in your opponent's
Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost"* and attack.ts resolves it through `effectiveRetreatCost`, saying so in
as many words: *"a Stadium that changes what it costs to retreat changes what these attacks hit for"*.
A printed reading here would make **one printed noun phrase mean two different things in two readers of
one file** — and Spidops ex `sv01-019` exposes it single-handed, because its "Trap Territory" Ability
RAISES the opponent's Retreat Cost while its "Wire Hang" SCALES off it, and the engine has made those
two meet since 0.61.0.

⑵ **THE RULES MAKE RETREAT COST A CURRENT VALUE, NOT A CONSTANT.** `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §11
defines the cost off the printed symbols and records that effects reduce it, but is **SILENT** on what
a card TEXT naming *"the Retreat Cost"* reads — so this went to the web, D373's route when the local
doc is silent. The official account states an **ORDER OF OPERATIONS** over the value (increases first,
then reductions; a Pokémon left with no Retreat Cost by an effect overrides every increase), which is
arithmetic over something that CHANGES, and both halves are already inside `effectiveRetreatCost`.
**A PRINTED CONSTANT WOULD NEED NO ORDER OF OPERATIONS AT ALL.**

⑶ 🛑 **AND IT IS THE READING WITH A FALSIFIER, WHICH IS THE GROUND THAT ACTUALLY SETTLES IT.**
**Flipping the arm to `retreatCostOf(spot.card)` turns FIVE cases RED, in BOTH directions** — measured
by doing it, before the build was trusted, and reverted by copy-back rather than by git.

🛑 **A GUARD THAT ONLY EXERCISES BOARDS WHERE THE TWO READINGS AGREE IS EXACTLY THE VACUOUS GUARD THIS
REPO KEEPS REDISCOVERING (D200 → D214).** So the disagreement is DRIVEN, in both directions, on four
real boards:

  Wasteland `sv02-175`** (the Stadium term) folds to {C}{C} and pays 220 where the printed column says

  `sv01-167`** folds to {C} and pays 110 where the printed column says 220. **A WRONG BUILD READING

A real-game ruling would have beaten any engine convention outright. **THERE IS NONE,

actually chosen**, which is why it is argued in the member's doc block instead of copied

**🛑 THE HEADLINE — A QUANTIFIER CONTRASTED AGAINST ITS OWN ABSENCE IS WHAT TURNS

**`choosePokemon` WAS THE ONE PROMPT KIND IN THE UNION WITH NO WAY TO SAY NO.** `chooseCards` has carried the distinction since it was written — *"`min: 0` — the printed 'up to' … Taking none is a legal answer"* against *"`min === max` — a MANDATORY exact pick, where the only decision is WHICH cards and never whether"* — `choosePokemonMulti` carries `declinable` for the printed *"you may"*, and `moveEnergy` and `attachCards` both document an empty answer as a legal decline. `attachEnergyFrom` is the one attach route that takes a prompt kind without it, so **every printed *"attach up to N"* it serves was resolved as an EXACT N**. Declinability was never a property of PARKING; it is a property of the PROMPT KIND, and this one was the hole.

Four independent lines, none of them these cards: (1) `ptcg-rules.md` §9.1 verbatim — *"'Search your deck for **up to 2** Basic Energy cards' (Earthen Vessel) — one, two, or none, all legal"*; (2) §9.1 also disposes of the *"you may"* — on an ACTIVATED Ability it *"is spent by choosing to use the Ability at all, so it adds nothing to the choice that follows"*, and a printed "you may" *"adds the empty answer, and only that one"*; (3) the catalog CONTRASTS the quantifier against its own absence on the same op and the same zone — N's PP Up `sv09-153` prints a bare *"Attach"*, Ethan's Ho-Oh prints *"up to 2"*; (4) `chooseCards`' own prompt doc had already classified the pair at the FIRST park kind this engine built.

### 2026-08-17 — build session #297 (P3-M5 — D357, a code-review repair whose first finding was a correctness defect already on `main`)

**FOUR REVIEW FINDINGS, FOUR FIXED, ZERO REFUSED.**

**FINDING 1 — THE DEFECT.** D356 gated Magearna `sv09-107`'s opening clause — *"**As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot,** whenever you attach an Energy card from your hand to 1 of your Pokémon, heal 90 damage from that Pokémon."* — on `target.spot === "active"` against the board `sweepTriggers` was WALKING. At the §6.2 attach that is the board **after** §6.1's Jet Energy `switchIfBenched` rider has already moved a body into the Active Spot, and the rider is a rider on **the same moment**, not a later action. Both directions were wrong on real boards, and both are now driven:

* **(a)** attaching Jet Energy `sv02-190` to a BENCHED damaged Magearna promoted it and THEN fired Auto Heal — ABILITY_TRIGGERED + HEALED, 80 → 0 — off a bearer that was on the Bench when the Energy landed.
* **(b)** with Magearna ACTIVE, attaching Jet to a damaged benched body DEMOTED it first and the printed 90 was **SILENTLY LOST**: zero HEALED rows under *either* ordering of the two simultaneous turn-player triggers. **There is no ordering that produces it**, which is the difference between a wrong answer and a debatable one.

Both were **verified RED against the D356 gate before the fix landed**. A regression case that was never seen to fail is a description, not a test.

**THE RULES QUESTION WAS SETTLED FROM THE CATALOG.** The Active-Spot clause reads the board **at the moment the trigger names**. (1) The one other TRIGGERED `activeOnly` family whose moment carries a board change says so IN PRINT — *"If this Pokémon **is in the Active Spot** and is damaged by an attack … (**even if this Pokémon is Knocked Out**)"*; the parenthetical exists to say a board change arriving WITH the trigger does not unmake a gate that held at the moment, and a Knock Out is a larger change than a switch. (2) The Checkup family names gate and moment in one breath. (3) Every remaining `activeOnly` printing is CONTINUOUS or ACTIVATED and has no second board to be read against — **no printing in the pool pairs an Active-Spot clause with a switch rider on its own moment**, which is why the question had never been forced.

🛑 **AND THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY IN THE REPO, HALF-APPLIED.** `bodyHoldingEnergy` keys the SUBJECT on the Energy so as to be *"right in both orders"* — it had already recognised Jet's switch and this trigger as two effects answering ONE moment whose order is the turn player's choice. D356 read that comment, applied it to the subject, and never asked it of the bearer gate one clause to the left. **A COMMENT THAT SOLVES HALF A PROBLEM IS THE MOST DANGEROUS KIND.**

**THE FIX**: `atMoment` threaded to both watched entry points, compared BY UID (a spot is a POSITION; the print names a BODY); `turn.ts` captures `atAttach` BEFORE the riders. The SUBJECT still reads the CURRENT board and must — **an antecedent is fixed when the moment happens, a pronoun is resolved when the consequent runs** — which is why one driven case covers both halves. `runBoardTrigger` and `damagedByAttackAbility` are unchanged, MEASURED: no rider sits between their moment and their gate.

🛑🛑 **THE FINDING WITH THE WIDEST REACH: A ROW COUNT IS NOT A COVERAGE MAP.** `sweepTriggers` carried two mutation rows after D356 and **neither touched the `activeOnly` gate** — the one line in it that reads a BOARD to answer a printed clause. The defect lived on an **unmutated line of a function that already had coverage**.

**FINDINGS 2-4.** (2) `energyCoin.test.ts` §6's baton was two TAUTOLOGIES; **a width-1 contiguity claim has no content**, and `xBoot.test.ts` §6 carried the identical pair — **a defect in a hand-off idiom propagates along the hand-off**. Both replaced with falsifiable permanent rungs, not deleted. (3) D356's name-rot sweep missed a third site **in a file it had already opened** and recorded itself as complete; **a coverage claim rots exactly like a count**, and the check neither pass ran is to grep the WRONG name to ZERO. (4) A mutant's `what` described its sibling row.

**AND TWO INHERITED FIGURES WERE RE-MEASURED AND BOTH WERE WRONG.** `stepOp`'s recorded 85,785 bytes matches no natural span (body 85,618 / +braced return type 85,702 / from the keyword 85,827) while its **58 rows reproduce exactly** — a byte figure is span-dependent and was recorded without its span. ### 2026-08-16 — build session #294 (P3-M5 — D354, the printed union of target types, and a refusal that had priced the wrong reading)

**P3-M5 — D354, *THE PRINTED UNION OF TARGET TYPES: AN ATTACH LEARNS THAT "YOUR {P} POKÉMON AND {M} POKÉMON" IS ONE SET.***

**BUILT: Steven's Metagross ex `sv10-145` "X-Boot"** — *"Once during your turn, you
may search your deck for a Basic {P} Energy card, a Basic {M} Energy card, or 1 of
each and attach them to your **{P} Pokémon and {M} Pokémon** in any way you like.
Then, shuffle your deck."* **1 printing / 1 card / 1 sentence / `legal_standard = 1`
— the ENTIRE Standard-legal population of the two-type attach target over all three
text columns.** Backlog row 10's `abilityIds` closes to zero; `ROWS`' non-attack
residue falls **8 → 7**.

#### 🛑🛑 THE FINDING — a refusal can name a true obstacle, quote a real price, and still have priced the wrong SENTENCE

D351 refused this card in two places, on reasoning that was **true in every
clause**: *"`AttachTargetRiders.targetType` is a single `string`"*. Row 10's own
cell priced it as *"two different `targetType`s in one sentence"*.

**That price is an answer to the PAIRING reading — and the pairing reading is
FREE.** Two `attachFromDeck` ops, each with its own single-`string` `targetType`,
spell "the {P} Energy onto a {P} body, the {M} onto a {M} body" for zero engine
diff. Only the UNION reading — one target set, `{P} ∪ {M}`, over which both found
cards distribute — costs anything at all.

**Which reading the card prints is a RULES question, not an engine one**, so it was
settled from the CATALOG before a line was written (remote D1 `luminous`,
2026-08-16, `json_each` keyed on `$.effect`, extractor verified against
known-present rows first):

1. **THE TEMPLATE.** *"attach them to `<NOUN>` in any way you like"* is **31
   printings**, and the `<NOUN>` slot holds **exactly one set description** in every
   one — "your Pokémon" ×24, "your Future Pokémon" ×2, "your Benched Pokémon",
   "your Marnie's Pokémon", "your Tera Pokémon", and X-Boot's. **NO PAIRING FORM
   EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE CATALOG.**
2. **THE CONSTRUCTION.** *"your {X} Pokémon and {Y} Pokémon"* appears on exactly
   **two** cards: this one and Lilligant `sv09-007`, whose sentence admits **no
   pairing reading at all**.

**A PRICE IS AN ANSWER TO A READING, AND THE READING IS USUALLY LEFT IMPLICIT.**
D353 found that a refusal re-verifying its own premise audits the wrong thing;
this is the layer under it — the premise can be sound and attached to the wrong
reading of the print.

#### THE ENGINE DIFF — one widened key and one normaliser

`AttachTargetRiders.targetType?: string` → **`string | readonly string[]`**. A
SECOND key (`targetTypes?`) is refused by this repo's own standing rule, written on
`attachFromTop.restTo` (D335/D352): *"two keys on one axis can be set to contradict
each other and no reading of the print says what the contradiction means."* The
precedent for ONE key widened to carry a second reading is in the same op family,
`attachFromTop.max: number | "any"`. `targetTypeNames` normalises both spellings
once for the two readers that care — the eligibility gate and the prompt caption —
so they cannot drift; the caption REPEATS the noun because the card does, and is

## 🛑 `bunx biome format` IS **NOT** CLEAN ON THIS REPO, AND MUST NEVER BE `--write`n

A finding worth recording because the checklist says *"run the anchor loop again
after biome touches anything"* and invites the wrong command. `bun run check`
runs **`biome lint . --error-on-warnings`**, which is clean. `bunx biome format .`
reports **188 pre-existing differences across 635 files** and always has. A
`format --write` here would rewrite the entire repo and break mutation anchors by
the hundred — the exact "line MOVED, not edited" failure the anchor loop exists
to catch, inflicted deliberately. **This session ran biome READ-ONLY, confirmed
`git status` was byte-clean afterwards, and therefore owed no second anchor
pass.** `lint --write` is a no-op at this head.
