#### 🛑🛑 The transferable finding: a row's own PATTERN is not always the clause its residue is blocked on

D340's rule is *census the SENTENCE, not the card*. This slice is that rule at one
further remove. Row 10's predicate is *"search your deck for … Energy … attach"*; what
actually gated these three ids was the **trigger clause in front of it**, and that
clause's other half lived in `attacks_json` — a column row 10 never looks at, because
row 10's attack half was closed at D235. **Census the sentence, and then census the
sentence the sentence rests on.**

#### 🛑 The design call: a named exception to `playableIf`'s own doc, and the exception is the CONJUNCTION

`registry.ts`'s `playableIf` doc block forbids per-body predicates — *"`conditionHolds`
takes a seat and no uid, so a self-pronoun has no referent in it"* — and counts NINE
legal printings excluded on that ground. The rule is right; this card is the one shape
it does not cover. **`activeOnly: true` gives the self-pronoun its referent**: it pins
the Ability's host to the single body `conditionHolds` reads, so *"your Active moved up
this turn"* ∧ *"this Pokémon IS the Active"* is exactly *"this Pokémon moved up this
turn"*, for every seat, consumer and phase (D124's own totality argument — the stamp is
on the Pokémon). The nine stay excluded because none of them names the Active Spot:
`activeOnly` is what would have to be TRUE of them, not what happens to be.

**D310's standing question is therefore ANSWERED, and the answer is NO.**
`remainingHpAtMost`'s doc has said since D310 that *"when the second per-body printing
lands, THAT is the slice that generalises this"*. This is not that printing, and the
answer is recorded **in that doc block** rather than left to be re-asked — D346's
spent-note rule applied to a spent QUESTION.

#### ⭐ The standing open finding's own check already existed, and it worked

`flipTheScript.test.ts` pins `playableIf`'s whole authored population **BY ID** over
`registryCardIds()`. It went RED on this build (**5 → 8 ids**) and forced the correction
of `registry.ts`'s prose (*"that leaves the 3 Fezandipiti ex printings as this field's
whole legal population today"*) in the same session. **A POPULATION PINNED BY ID IS A
PROSE FIGURE THAT CANNOT ROT SILENTLY** — the cheap, narrow guard D343, D344, D345 and
D346 each proposed and none built, sitting in the tree since D275.

⚠️ **And it was this slice's biggest prediction miss, in exactly the shape the standing
lesson warns about.** The prediction grepped `playableIf` across NON-test files, found
the doc block and correctly predicted the prose repair — and never ran the prescribed
`grep -rn "<NAME>" packages/engine/src/*.test.ts | grep "expect("` on it, because the
figure list was built from *census constants* and `playableIf` was filed as *a field*.
**A FIELD NAME IS A FIGURE NAME TOO: run the standing grep over every identifier the
build TOUCHES, not only over every number the build MOVES.**

#### 🛑 What was refused, measured rather than priced

D346 left one specific instruction: *"the `attacks_json` half of the 'in any way you
like' clause is 36 legal printings on 36 sentences and wholly unpriced — census what the
readers already resolve before pricing any of it."* Run literally, it is **two defects
deep**:

* **A UNIT DEFECT** (D341's lesson). `36 sentences` is `COUNT(DISTINCT attacks_json)` —
  whole JSON blobs, one per printing. It is the PRINTING count wearing a SENTENCE
  count's name. Re-grouped through `json_each`: **20 sentences / 36 legal printings**.
* **RUNG 1 RETURNS ZERO** (D263's lesson, the one D346 asked for by name). The nine
  exported readers ALREADY resolve **8 of the 20 sentences / 17 of the 36 printings**,
  every one through `deriveAttackEffect`. The unpriced residue is **12 sentences / 19
  printings** across at least SIX mechanisms — a damage-counter SPREAD (3 sentences / 8
  printings: Dragapult ex ×4, Flutter Mane ×3, Sinistcha ×1), an energy-move "in any
  way" (3/3), the Future/Tera subgroup targets (3/4), an OPPONENT's-discard source
  (1/1), a coin-COUNTED attach (1/1) and a damage-counter MOVE (1/1). The largest
  coherent block needs a counter DISTRIBUTION park — a new prompt kind — and **every
  sub-block is smaller than this row's 3.**

**A CENSUS FIGURE'S UNIT ROTS FASTER THAN ITS COUNT, and a `COUNT(DISTINCT <json
column>)` is always a printing count.**

Also refused: Steven's Metagross ex `sv10-145` (the *"or 1 of each"* grammar AND two
`targetType`s in one sentence) and Energy Coin `sv10.5b-081` (1 printing behind a
two-coin AND gate).

#### ⚠️ The recorded limitation, flagged AND driven

The print is a MOMENT (*"when this Pokémon moves"*) and this models it as a GATE
re-checked at use time. They differ on exactly one board — a body that moves up and is
switched back DOWN in the same turn loses the use. The divergence REFUSES rather than
affords (D222's direction), it takes two switch effects in one turn to reach, and buying
the literal reading costs a new `TriggerTiming` plus an optional-trigger confirm — a
mechanism authored on the evidence of a board no printing rewards. `buzzingBoost.test.ts`
§6 drives it, so it is a measured decision and not an unknown.

### 2026-08-15 — build session #286 (P3-M5 — D346, the zero-diff row a REWRITTEN residue note hid, and the third direction a work order can rot)

**Slice D346.** Engine **0.251.0 → 0.252.0**, ONE bump over FIVE sites, in ONE

discard pile to your {L} Pokémon **in any way you like**. If you use this
Ability, this Pokémon is Knocked Out."* **3 Standard-legal printings, ONE
sentence, ONE program object, and a ZERO ENGINE DIFF** — `registry.ts` is the
entire build, the first row in five slices to cost no engine line at all.

#### The method, run in order for the third slice running

1. **Largest live `ROWS` residue**, read off `censusAtHead.test.ts` rather than

   | column | printings | legal | sentences |

   | `effect` | 3 | 1 | 2 |

   | `attacks_json` | 59 | 36 | 36 |

#### 🛑🛑 The finding: a residue note can rot by being REWRITTEN

`legalNonAttackPrograms.test.ts` has priced this card **correctly since D263**:

> *"Magneton … the attach **IS EXPRESSIBLE** (3 ops, `targetType: "Lightning"`),
> but the second printed clause is 'If you use this Ability, this Pokémon is
> Knocked Out' and NO OP IN THE ENGINE KNOCKS OUT ITS OWN HOST. Grepped, not
> assumed."*

D345 shipped `knockOutSelf` — spending precisely that blocker — and then wrote a
**new** residue note saying the blocker was the *"in any way you like"*
DISTRIBUTION and that the card needed "a multi-destination assignment prompt",
propagating it to **NINE FILES**. That claim was false when it was written and
had been false since D263, which built the identical clause on Archaludon ex as
**two** `attachEnergyFrom` ops. **The card was buildable at D345's own head.**

⚠️ **D341 and D344 each found a residue note that rotted by STANDING STILL while
the code moved. This one rotted by being REWRITTEN, and that is the more
expensive half.** A stale note disagrees with the code, so re-derivation catches
it and the code wins. A rewritten note disagrees with **nothing**: it carries a
fresh decision's authority, cites a real mechanism by name, and routes the next
slice past a card that is already buildable. **WHEN A SLICE SPENDS A BLOCKER,
DELETE THE NOTE THAT NAMED IT** — do not re-point it at the next mechanism that
comes to mind without re-running the method's step (3) against the code.

This is the **third direction** a work order can rot. D263 recorded the first
two: a row that gets BUILT and is not removed (an assertion catches it), and a
row whose PIECE is bought by a slice that never opens the file (nothing catches
it). The third is caught by nothing either, and unlike the second it looks
**fresher** than the truth.

#### D345's open question, answered from source: **NEITHER**

It asked whether `attachEnergyFrom` can reach the existing `attachCards`
assignment prompt "rather than whether a new prompt is needed". It must reach
neither, and the engine had said so in three places before the question was
asked:

* `effects.ts` `attachEnergyFrom.count` — *"N ops park N times and may land on N
  different bodies (Koraidon 'Dino Cry''s printed **in any way you like**), where
  `count` parks ONCE and pins the batch."*
* `effects.ts` `attachFromHand` — the `attachCards` MAP exists for *"any
  NUMBER"*, which *"names no unit, so … there is no N to unroll"*; the two
  `sv08-079`/`-204` printings that DO spell a count *"are already built, as 2
  separate `attachEnergyFrom` ops"*.
* `registry.ts` `ASSEMBLE_ALLOY` (D263) — two ops, deliberately **not**
  `count: 2`, written as the expansion `attachFromZoneProgram` already emits for
  the ATTACK half of the same family.

**Magneton prints "up to 3". It is three ops.**

#### The nine-file doctrine repair (D343's rule)

Falsifying *"Magneton owes a second mechanism"* meant grepping every site that
states it — **nine files**, where D343's record for one falsified doctrine was
eight across six: `registry.ts`, `effects.ts`, `interpreter.ts`, `index.ts`,

#### One design call, flagged rather than hidden

`programPlayable` refuses an `attachEnergyFrom` whose source zone holds no
matching Energy **or** whose target set is empty. So a Magneton with no Basic
Energy in the discard cannot use the Ability at all, where the printed rules
would let you use it and die for nothing. **D222's afford-then-reject wins**,
because this program's other clause is a COST and not an effect — there is no
"first half of what it prints" left to do, the way Giovanni's bare switch is.
`overvoltDischarge.test.ts` §5 drives the refusal and names the one gate a later
slice would change.

⚠️ **And the gate's `targetType` arm is UNREACHABLE on this card**, which is a
fact about the print rather than an untested branch: the destination is *"your
{L} Pokémon"* and Magneton is itself {L}, so any board that can use the Ability
holds at least one legal target — the host. Written out and driven.

### 🛑 THE ROW FOUND A LIVE DEFECT IN A GATE, NOT ONLY A GAP IN A CATALOG

`programPlayable` (cardplay.ts) refused to play an Ability whose first op is a
`damageChosen` whenever the opponent's **BENCH** was empty. That is the
`opponentBench` reading and only that one. It had been **accidentally right for
two hundred decisions**, because every REGISTRY producer of the op was a Bench
snipe (Hawlucha, Meowscarada ex, Radiant Blastoise) and every `opponentAny`
producer was an **ATTACK** — and attacks never consult that function (§8, and
D247 had already written that zero down). Cursed Blast is the first registry
`opponentAny` row, and an opponent holding a bare Active greyed out an Ability
whose own op offers that Active as a candidate.

Fixed by sharing the op's own funnel — `snipeTargets`, exported for exactly the
reason `gustTargets` is, so the refusal and the offer read one predicate.
**A PREDICATE RE-IMPLEMENTED BESIDE ITS OP IS RIGHT UNTIL THE OP GROWS AN ARM** —
which is the insertion-order rung's lesson wearing a different hat, and this slice
paid both in one afternoon.

### THE ENGINE DIFF, AND WHY THE OP HAS NO FIELDS

`knockOutSelf` is **field-free**: the clause is byte-identical across all three
sentences that print it, so there is nothing for a field to vary over (D104's
minimal-shape rule). It **marks rather than kills** — §8.1's sweep is
`lethalRefs → planPrizes → knockOut` and is already owed to every settled program
by `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts`, so the op writes the one thing the sweep reads
(`damage >= effectiveMaxHp`) and stops. `returnSelf` has ridden that seam since
D311; this is its second consumer and the first that pays a Prize.

The KO is **not damage**: no Weakness/Resistance, no reduction passive, no
prevention, and no event of its own — a `COUNTERS_PLACED` row would say the host
took counters, which is exactly what the printed clause is not.

### ⚠️ ONE TEST WAS VACUOUS UNTIL THE ATTRIBUTION QUESTION WAS ASKED OF IT

The HP-aura case ("the maximum is read AT THE MOMENT THE OP RUNS") was first
written against an invented `fix-*` body carrying Ability TEXT and **no program**
— which raises nobody's maximum. The Dusclops would have died of its printed 90
with the assertion looking satisfied. It is now the REAL Ludicolo `sv09-037`
(D324's `seatHpBonus`, +40 seat-wide), with `programFor` asserted DEFINED first
and the Knock Out asserted BY UID. **A fixture that carries the words is not a
fixture that carries the mechanism** — the same defect this repo has now caught
nine times, found here in this slice's own new file.

🛑🛑 **THE `or` WAS PRICED AS "NEITHER A CAPTION NOR A PROMPT KIND", AND THE KIND
HALF TURNED OUT TO BE ALREADY PAID.** `confirm`'s own doc block settles it: *"a
confirm answer means run `then` … a fact about the program"*, where a `mayDraw`
answer is a fact about cards. **A binary answer that picks between two printed
arms is a MEANING this engine has had since D186**, and `optional { then,
otherwise }` has been a two-armed branch on a human answer since D316.

🛑 **AND IT IS REFUSED ANYWAY, FROM THE SOURCE RATHER THAN FROM TASTE.** An
`optional` parks `{kind:"confirm", note}` and **a confirm carries NO CANDIDATES**.
The print hands the information over FIRST — *"**Look at the top 3 cards** of your
deck **and** put them back in any order, or …"* — so an `optional` wrapper asks
the question **BLIND**. That is not a caption difference; it is the loss of the
one thing the sentence gives before it asks. **THE PROMPT THAT ASKS THE `or` HAS
TO BE THE PROMPT THAT DELIVERS THE LOOK**, and `orderCards` (D341) is the only
prompt whose window `redactPrompt` resolves to the answerer alone.

**THE ANSWER IS THE EMPTY ORDERING**, and it reads as the print does: *none of
these cards is being put back on top.* It is a value the prompt could not
previously hold rather than one taken away from something else — `validateChoice`
demands a permutation of a window never smaller than 2 — and it is admitted
EXACTLY when `alt` is present. ⭐ **`applyChoice` NEEDED NO ARM AT ALL**: both of
its splices reduce to the identity on an empty answer, so the WHOLE of the second
arm is the `continuationOps` splice. **D316's shape exactly — the yes/no
difference lives in `resumeProgram`, never in the apply.**

**THE PIECES.** 1 new `EffectOp` (`bottomDeckTop {n}` — shuffle the top `n`,
append under the deck) + 2 optional op fields (`reorderTop.otherwise`,
`.otherwiseNote`) + 1 optional prompt field (`orderCards.alt`) + 1
`continuationOps` member (**the FIFTH, and the first branch carrier that is not a
gate**) + 1 `GameEvent` (`DECK_TOP_TO_BOTTOM`, count-only, **no `actor`** — D135,
the op has one seat) + 1 `log.ts` row + 1 wire field + 2 dialog buttons + 1
registry row + 1 driven suite. **0 new prompt kinds, 0 new choice kinds, 0
`validateChoice` arms, 0 `applyChoice` arms, 0 `redactPrompt` arms, 0
`ONE_PER_KIND` rows.**

⚠️ **`otherwise` IS A FLAT `EffectOp[]` AND THAT IS CORRECTNESS, NOT STYLE.**
`subPrograms` discovers sub-programs by a NEGATIVE predicate over an op's own
ARRAY-VALUED properties, and its doc names the one thing it cannot see: *"a
program reached through a field that is NOT an `EffectOp[]`"*. A nested
`{note, ops}` object would have hidden this arm from `walkProgram` and opened a
**FOURTH instance of the population defect D341, D342 and D343 each repaired —
and the first one that would have been AUTHORED rather than inherited.** The
carrier pin proved the choice from the other side: it went red naming
`["reorderTop", ["otherwise"]]` before the suite that drives the card existed,
which is the first time in that pin's history that the union actually grew a
fifth branching op.

⚠️ **THE M1 GUARD NEEDED NO SECOND ARM, AND THAT IS ARITHMETIC.** `top.length` is
`min(n, deck.length)`, so for any `n ≥ 2` the existing `top.length < 2` refusal is
exactly *"both arms are the same state"*: a 0- or 1-card deck shuffled onto the
bottom of what remains of it is where it was. The only board separating the two
tests is `n === 1` over a long deck, which no printed sentence spells. Pinned from
both sides by 1-card, 2-card and empty-deck rungs.

🛑 **THE PROSE SWEEP: FIVE SITES, AND ONE HAD BEEN FALSE SINCE D341 WITH NOTHING
TO SAY SO.** Census row 11's note still called `sv08-171` *"the ORDERED answer no
prompt in this engine has"* — two slices after D341 shipped that prompt. The id

### 2026-08-15 — build session #283 (P3-M5 — D343, Kofu's printed "in any order": `reorderTop` learns the deck's bottom, and the row the work order priced had already shipped)

**Slice D343.** Engine **0.248.0 → 0.249.0**, ONE bump over FOUR sites.
`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 20**.

⚠️ **THIS SESSION RAN IN TWO HALVES ACROSS A CONTAINER RESTART.** The first half
built the row, wrote the mutant corpus, fixed the errand and bumped the version —
four commits, all pushed. It was killed roughly fifteen minutes into its mutation
sweep, and the sweep and the entire docs close-out died with it. The second half
re-verified the head, re-derived every census figure from source, graded the
prediction, found and repaired one further defect, ran the sweep to completion and
wrote this entry. **The engine work survived because it was committed as it
landed; the sweep did not because it was left for last.** That is the whole
argument for the commit rhythm, stated by the one slice it happened to.

#### 🛑 The row was already built, and the work order did not know

`registry.ts` held `const KOFU` at `5827be3`, wired at `"sv07-138"`, `"sv07-165"`
and `"fix-kofu"`, with a doc block, a demonstrator in `FIXTURE_POOL`, a row in
`legalNonAttackPrograms.test.ts`'s table and two driven tests. D341's resume point
offered it as one of three unbuilt candidates and priced it at 2 legal printings.
**It had shipped.** That is **D330's lesson at its second site**: a backlog row
that names a card is a claim about the tree, and it rots exactly like a count.

What was *not* built is the printed **"in any order"**, and the program dropped it
in silence:

```
{ op: "payFromHand", count: 2, to: "deckBottom", recordAs: "paid" },
{ op: "recordGate", slot: "paid", then: [{ op: "drawCards", count: 4 }] },
```

**THE TELL WAS IN THE EXISTING TEST, AND IT IS D342's SHAPE EXACTLY.** The suite
asserted the payment landed with
`expect([...tail].sort()).toEqual([...picks].sort())` — it **SORTS**. It asserts a
**SET** where the print demands a **SEQUENCE**. D342 found its two survivors were
"an assertion about a FIELD instead of about a BOARD"; this is the sibling one
abstraction over, and it is why a card that has been green for many slices was
wrong about the only clause this row exists for.

#### The decision: a WINDOW FORK, not a CHANNEL — and two refusals from source

`reorderTop` read and wrote the deck's TOP and could not address the other end
(`interpreter.ts` park `deck.slice(0, n)`, apply `[...choice.uids, ...rest]`). So
D342's search→`deckTop`→`reorderTop` channel was unavailable, and the resume point
recorded "the channel is the board is NOT available here."

🆕 **THAT IS WRONG IN ITS GENERALITY AND RIGHT IN ITS PARTICULARS.** After
`payFromHand{to:"deckBottom"}` the two paid cards **ARE the deck's last two, by
construction** — the same by-construction guarantee that made D342's trick work,
read at the other end. **D342's TRICK IS GENERAL; ITS READER WAS NOT.** The cost
of the row is one window fork, not one channel:

```
{ op: "reorderTop", n: 2, from: "bottom" }
```

placed **inside the existing `recordGate{slot:"paid"}`**, ahead of the draw —
`recordGateHolds` is `filed.length > 0`, so a run that paid nothing never opens an
ordering window over two cards nobody put there.

**TWO CHEAPER OPTIONS WERE REFUSED, AND BOTH REFUSALS ARE READ OUT OF THE SOURCE
RATHER THAN ARGUED FROM TASTE:**

* **REFUSED — let the `chooseCards` answer's ARRAY ORDER be the ordering.**
  Superficially free: `payFromHandApply` already builds `paid` by iterating the
  answer's `uids`, so the order is *incidentally* consumed today. Refused on two
  independent facts. (1) `index.ts`'s D341 block states the doctrine this would
  break — *"every `chooseCards` consumer iterates the answer to MOVE cards, so
  two answers naming the same uids are the same board, and the validator is free
  to treat the array as a set."* A client is **licensed** to reorder that answer.
  (2) `payFromHand` **AUTO-RESOLVES when `candidates.length <= op.count`** — on
  the exactly-two-other-cards board that is the *commonest* Kofu line, **no prompt
  is shown at all** and the cards land in raw hand order. The printed clause is
  not merely unspecified there; it is **ABSENT**. That branch is correct for every
  printing authored before this one and false for this one.
* **REFUSED — a prompt over the HAND, before the move.** It must both SELECT a
  subset and SEQUENCE it. Neither `chooseCards` (subset, no order) nor
  `orderCards` (permutation of the *whole* offer) does both, so it is a **new
  prompt kind** and re-pays D341's entire bill — kind, choice kind, validator,
  redact, zod, projection, two dialogs and the `ONE_PER_KIND` pin. Its cheap
  variant, a second park fed by the `paid` RECORD, is **buying a channel when the
  board is one**, which is the exact thing D342 says to check first.

⚠️ **THE FLOOR/DOMAIN HAZARD IS D342's `exact`, ONE ZONE OVER, WITH A WEAKER
GUARANTEE, AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER.** `reorderTop{n:2}`'s
domain is 2; `payFromHand`'s floor is `min(handSize, 2)`. They agree only because
`handCostUnmet` refuses the play unless two are payable — **a gate in another
file**, not a property of the op pair. D342's `exact` made its pair
self-sufficient; this one is not.

`DECK_TOP_REORDERED { seat, actor, count }` gains **`end?: "bottom"`** — OPTIONAL,
absent on every existing construction site. One op with a window fork owes one row
with a window fork (D341's reason for making `side` a field). The optionality is
load-bearing and it is what keeps `derivedReorderTop.test.ts`'s two exact-shape
`toEqual({ type, seat, actor, count })` assertions green **unedited** — a REQUIRED
field would have reddened both.

**The row still fires on the bottom fork**, D241's rule kept unconditional. The
tempting "there is no look, so emit nothing" is refused: it is true of *Kofu* (the
controller put those two cards there themselves, one op earlier) and false of the
*fork* (a future "look at the bottom 3 cards…" is a real look), so gating an EVENT
on `from` would key a confidentiality rule on a window.

`MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` **STAYS 20**: events are rendered into `record.log` rows and
are not themselves persisted, and a new optional op field is registry-side program
vocabulary.

#### 🛑🛑 The price was wrong in its one hard clause, and the correction is the finding

D341's resume point priced this row as needing *"a `searchDeck` whose PICKS are
then sequenced onto the deck — i.e. the `orderCards` prompt parked a second time
… **what is new is a prompt whose candidates are the previous answer, which no op
in this engine does yet.**"*

The first half is exactly right. The second half is **false at this head**, and
its falseness is the whole reason the row cost what it did.

**THE CHANNEL IS THE DECK.** Once `searchDeck { dest: "deckTop" }` has put the
picks on top, `reorderTop { n: 2 }`'s candidates are `deck.slice(0, 2)` — which
ARE the picks, by construction, with nothing carried across the park and no
`continuationOps` member. And a PROGRAM has parked twice since **D186**
(`resumeProgram` → `runProgram(rest)`, Koraidon "Dino Cry"); what is true is the
narrower statement D216 corrected D206 into, that **one OP** gets one park.

> 🆕 **"NO OP DOES THIS YET" IS A CLAIM ABOUT OPS, AND A PROGRAM IS NOT AN OP.**
> Every previous re-pricing of this family asked what a single op could carry
> between two questions. It does not have to carry anything: the ZONE between the
> two ops already holds it. **BEFORE BUYING A CHANNEL BETWEEN TWO PARKS, CHECK
> WHETHER THE BOARD IS ONE.**

#### The cost

    [{ op: "shuffleDeck" },
     { op: "searchDeck", filter: {kind:"anyCard"}, max: 2, exact: true, dest: "deckTop" },
     { op: "reorderTop", n: 2 }]

**0 new `EffectOp` · 0 new prompt kinds · 0 new choice kinds · 0
`continuationOps` members · 1 new `dest` inhabitant · 1 new optional op field.**
Plus one anchor (`ATTACK_SEARCH_TOP_ORDER`), one shared factory
(`searchTopOrderProgram`), one `searchMove` arm, one caption arm, one
`DECK_SEARCHED` inhabitant, one `log.ts` row, one zod member and one
`CHOOSE_CARDS_VERB` cell.

**It is a `dest` rather than a new op, and that is the price difference the row
turned on.** A `searchDeckToTop` op would have bought the identical board and one
extra row in every op-keyed auditor table in the repo — which is why
`classified.size` (39) and `swept.size` (27) both stand still.

**The factory is SHARED, not transcribed.** The sentence is printed in two
columns; the deriver and the registry const call the same function, and the suite
asserts they are `toEqual` so the sharing is observable from outside rather than
only true by inspection. **A SENTENCE PRINTED IN TWO COLUMNS OWES ONE READING.**

#### 🛑 `exact` reads like a caption field and is a correctness field

Nobody priced it at all. At `searchDeck`'s standing `min: 0`, a player who
declines the search — or takes 1 of 2 — is then handed `reorderTop`'s window over
a top holding a card **they never searched for and were never shown**: an
information gain and a re-ordering the print does not grant. With the floor set
(clamped to `candidates.length`, D334's rule on `lookAtTopN`) the window is
exactly the picks, and a deck too short to fill it collapses on `reorderTop`'s own
`top.length < 2` guard. The print agrees — *"2 cards"*, no *"up to"*, no *"you
may"* — so the field is authored from the bytes and merely happens to also be
load-bearing, which is the order D334 wrote it in.

#### ⚠️ `shuffleDeck` leads where the print says second, and that is a proof

The print reads search → shuffle → place; the program reads shuffle →
search-and-place. Sound, because the search's answer is a SET of cards and never a
set of POSITIONS: `shuffle(deck) minus picks` and `shuffle(deck minus picks)` are
the same distribution (a uniform permutation restricted to a subset is uniform on
that subset). What the transposition BUYS is that `"deckTop"` stays a pure
destination — a `dest` that also shuffled could not spell *"…then put those cards
on top of it"* with no shuffle the day one prints.

THE HANDOFF IS MOST CONFIDENT ABOUT"** — the three summands came with a warning label
attached and were right; the reveal figure came with none and was wrong.

## 🛑 "Maushold ex" CONTAINS "Maushold" — THE PAIR OF CASES THAT IS THE WHOLE ROW

That prefix relation is why the card is printed as a disjunction at all, and it is the

already take every `Maushold ex`, the second member would be dead weight, and deleting it
would be invisible on every board.** So exactness is driven in BOTH directions, and the
cast carries two more bodies for it: `Mausholder` (a strict extension of neither printed
name, which a `startsWith` "fixed" by special-casing the `" ex"` suffix would still take)
and `Tandemaus` (the shared PRE-EVOLUTION, the near miss a *"search the family"* build
would take, since both printed members evolve from it). The offer is asserted as a SET —
exactly the two names out of a 60-card deck — rather than as three separate absences,
because three `.has(...) === false` checks all pass on a widening that admits some
fourth id none of them names.

*"the OPPONENT's board is untouched"* first asserted p2's deck length was unchanged and

the attack, which ENDS THE TURN, and p2 then draws for their own turn.** A length
equality across a turn boundary is not a claim about this op at all. Replaced with
CONTAINMENT plus PROVENANCE — nothing is added to p2's deck, p2's bench does not move,
every benched pick came out of *p1's* deck — plus an explicit `after.turn === parked.turn
+ 1` that makes the draw a stated fact instead of a hidden one. **STRICTLY SHARPER THAN
THE LINE IT REPLACES**, and "widen the board" would not have fixed it, because the board
was never too narrow — **the ASSERTION WAS FALSE** (D328's rule, met from the other side).

| split | **13** | the **READERS**, on the SPLIT string | **NO** — this sentence carries no gate clause |

`searchDeck.also?: readonly { filter: CardFilter; max: number }[]` — **a LIST where
`lookAtTopN.also` is a single PAIR**, same rule (D331: ship the arity the printing spells),
different answer, because this op's printing spells four. The census is the whole argument:
the resume point's inherited `instr(col,', and a ') > 0` is 3 rows / 3 legal, but the
SENTENCE form `instr(col,'earch your deck for') > 0 AND instr(col,' and a ') > 0` over all
three text columns returns **8 printings / 3 legal** — arity 2 at 5 printings / **0 legal**
(Arven `sv01-166`/`-235`/`-249`, `sv03-186`, `sv04.5-235`), arity 3 at 2 / 2, arity 4 at
1 / 1; `5 + 2 + 1 = 8` and `0 + 2 + 1 = 3` ✅. **THE ARITY AXIS STARTS AT TWO AND ITS TWO IS
ENTIRELY OUT OF STANDARD** (D187: a registry row is keyed by card id and legality is a hard
filter on it) — a pair field, the sibling op's shape, would have refused the FOUR that
Standard actually prints. ⚠️ **AND THE NEAR MISS IS A DIFFERENT GRAMMAR**:
`instr(abilities_json,'card, a ') > 0` is 4 rows / 4 legal and every one prints *"…, a Basic
{Y} Energy card, **or 1 of each**"* — a DISJUNCTION. A field spelled *"several filters, take
some"* would have claimed all four and got all four wrong.

It is a **NEW AXIS** rather than a value of an existing key (D335's standing test): not a
value of `filter`, because `anyOf` (D245) yields this candidate set for free and buys exactly
ONE flat cap; not a value of `max`, because `max` is a number and **a DISTRIBUTION over kinds
is not a number**. The first group stays `filter` + `max`, so **no existing row moves**.
Overlapping groups keep `lookAtTopN.also`'s conservative rule (a uid matching two filters
counts against BOTH caps) — transferred, not re-decided; every printed group here is disjoint
by construction, so no printed board can tell the readings apart.

## 🛑 THE INHERITED PRICE, FALSE IN ITS CHEAPEST CLAUSE FOR THE SIXTH SESSION RUNNING

Priced as *"`chooseCards.caps` is already a LIST for exactly this reason, so that slice buys
only its own op field."*

**TRUE half, and grepping sharpened it**: both readers of `caps` are arity-blind —
`validateChoice`'s `for (const cap of prompt.caps ?? [])` (cardplay.ts) and `GameHud`'s
`cappedOut` `.some(...)` — `redact.ts` and `projection.ts` copy the list whole, and
`packages/schema` gains no key. **The prompt half really was free.**

🛑 **FALSE half — "buys only its own op field", and the missing half was the CAPTION.**
`searchNote` took ONE filter and ONE number and had **no join at all**: `lookNote` was given
its two-noun join at D332 and this function never was. The op field feeds a PREDICATE *and* a
STRING, and D334's rule is that such a field owes BOTH arms. **WHAT IT ACTUALLY COST**:
`searchNote` went from **7 code lines to 24** (a changed signature — `groups` in place of one
`filter` — three arms where there was one, and a per-group `phrase` helper), inside a
32-code-line / 8-deletion `interpreter.ts` diff, plus **two of the twelve mutation rows** and
several of the 24 suite cases. Unpaid, this slice would have shipped *"Search your deck for up
to 3 Pokémon into your hand."* over Larry's Skill — the flat SUM against the FIRST group's
noun, the printed conjunction deleted — and it was **driven red by a case before it was
written**. 🛑 **AND THE SERIAL COMMA IS ITS OWN SUB-CLAUSE**: `lookNote` joins with a bare
`" and "`, which cannot spell *"A, B, and C"* at any arity. **A LIST FIELD DOES NOT INHERIT A
PAIR FIELD'S CAPTION.** The Oxford comma is the PRINT's — both cards carry it — so it is
reproduced rather than chosen, and the two-noun fallback is the same join with no commas,
which is what a legal Arven printing would want the day one exists.

🆕 **LESSON: "THE OTHER OP ALREADY DID THIS" IS A CLAIM ABOUT *ONE CONSUMER*.** D332 paid for
both halves of its own field; the price forwarded here remembered only the half that was hard
last time. **A SHARED PIECE IS SHARED PER READER, NOT PER OP — ENUMERATE THE READERS.**

**AND THE BENCH CLAMP MOVED TO THE SUM.** `benchSpace` is one number for the whole answer, so
it now binds the TOTAL rather than the first group's `max`. Both new rows are `dest: "hand"`,
so nothing printed can see it today; it is written against the sum rather than left to be
discovered by the first printing that benches several nouns.

## 🛑 THE UN-GREPPED CLAUSE, AND THE EVENT'S OWN SENTENCE IS THE ANSWER

The resume point flagged one thing: *which event do the leftovers ride*, warning that
`DECK_TOP_DISCARDED`'s producers are enumerated by name so a third **"may not be the right shape at
all"**. Grepping every occurrence returns the enumerations, and they say the opposite.

`effects.ts` refuses `DECK_TOP_DISCARDED` for this op's own `dest: "discard"` because *"here the
discard IS the printed decision"*, and the event's doc block defines its cards as the ones that
*"LEFT the deck without anyone deciding about them one at a time"*. **Leftovers are the definition
of the second clause.** So the sentence that refuses the event for one field is the argument for it
on the other, and the two discards on one op really do want two events — this op simply already had
the other one.

🆕 **THE SPLIT IS BY WHETHER A DECISION WAS MADE ABOUT THE CARD, NEVER BY WHERE IT ENDED UP.** One
op, one printing, two discards, two events: Rockruff's *"You may discard that card"* is a card the
player CHOSE, Explorer's Guidance's *"Discard the other cards"* is every card the player did not.
The rule is now printed once, in `events.ts`, where a fourth producer will read it.

✅ **AND THE FOURTH PATH COST THE RENDERER NOTHING**, which is the strongest evidence D153's
`actor === seat` comparison was the right key: a per-op flag would have owed a third case for a row
whose voice was already decided. The event is now **THREE ops and FOUR paths, splitting 3–1 on
agency**.

🛑 **SO THE PRICE'S "not free" HALF WAS RIGHT ABOUT PROSE AND WRONG ABOUT CODE.** No new event, no
new event field, no renderer arm, no `MATCH_RECORD_VERSION` move. What it cost was **SEVEN STALE
ENUMERATIONS ACROSS FOUR FILES**, none of which `tsc` can see: *"TWO ops produce this row"* and
*"Three paths"* (`events.ts`), *"TWO push sites, THREE paths"* and *"split 2–1 on agency"*
(`log.ts`), *"that event's two producers"* and *"the SECOND of the event's two push sites … two of
its THREE paths"* (`effects.ts`) — **and the seventh was a CASE NAME**, `log.test.ts`'s
*"END TO END: all three real producer paths"*.

🆕 🛑 **A COUNT IN A CASE NAME IS A MEASUREMENT OF THE BLOCK UNDER IT, SO IT IS REPAIRED WITH A
BOARD AND NEVER WITH A WORD.** Explorer's Guidance is DRIVEN there as the fourth path, off a real
deck, because a producer that wrote `actor: otherSeat(ctx.seat)` passes every assertion in the
synthetic `(seat, actor)` table above it and prints *"Ember had 4 cards discarded from the top of
their deck"* over a card Ember played on their own deck. That is the exact regression D153 split
that block in two to catch.

very same op**, one session later: a value that is equivalent as a predicate is not equivalent as a

already exists" IS A CLAIM ABOUT ONE CONSUMER, NOT ABOUT THE FIELD.**

🛑 **AND `min` IS THE FIRST FLOOR ON THIS PROMPT THAT A SHORT ZONE CAN MAKE UNANSWERABLE.**
`payFromHand`'s and `bottomFromOpponentHand`'s floors are gated upstream on a hand that holds the

`candidates.length`. 🆕 **`max` NEVER NEEDED THAT, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: a ceiling above
the candidate count cannot bind, which is exactly why D333's `"any"` could be resolved anywhere and
this could not.** A CEILING IS SAFE WHEN IT IS TOO HIGH; A FLOOR IS NOT.

call — so the Ability is not usable on that board and the wrong-body arm is **unreachable**. Pinned
through the REJECT, not through a board that never happens.

### 2026-08-13 — build session #269 (P3-M5 — D329, two declared survivors, both buildable, and a caveat that was a wrong answer)

**A DEBT-CLOSING SESSION, NOT A BUILD SLICE.** No new printing, no new op, no new field, no new
event, no registry row; `packages/schema` takes a zero diff. Three debts were handed over — two
DECLARED mutation survivors and one written-down edge in the KO sweep — with the instruction to
build the boards or prove they cannot exist.

🛑 **ALL THREE WERE UNDERPRICED IN THE SAME DIRECTION, AND THAT IS THE ONLY GENERAL THING HERE.**
Each was recorded as a **limit on what could be reached** — no suite can build that board, no
population exists, the fall-through owns it — and each turned out to be **reachable**. D328 was
scrupulous about saying which of its claims were untested; what it was not scrupulous about was
whether "untested" meant "untestable". 🛑 **A DECLARATION THAT SOMETHING CANNOT BE REACHED IS A
CLAIM LIKE ANY OTHER, AND IT IS THE ONE KIND OF CLAIM THE MUTATION HARNESS CANNOT FALSIFY FOR YOU
— it can only report the row surviving, which is exactly what the declaration predicts.**

**(1) `D328-retreat-sweep-runs-before-the-trigger` IS A STALE-SURVIVOR, AND ITS REASON WAS ABOUT A
CARD THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** The declaration asked for *"a board where `onActiveMovedToBench`
counters ALONE are lethal — Magcargo `sv05-029` `Lava Zone` on the opponent's side, against a
retreater already within its counters of dying"*, and turn.ts said the same thing at the call
(*"lands its counters on the body that MOVED … and puts them there"*, *"the counters that trigger
places are a second way this same move can turn lethal"*). **LAVA ZONE PLACES NO COUNTERS.** Its
printed consequent is *"their **new Active Pokémon** is now Burned"* and its program is one op,
`{ op: "applyStatus", target: "defender", status: "burned" }` — a DIFFERENT BODY from the one that
moved, a §12 condition rather than damage, and dealt at the Checkup. So the requested board is
unbuildable **and so is every board on which this trigger contributes lethality**; the retreat has
exactly ONE lethality source on today's pool and it is the cost.

⚠️ **THE ORDER IS STILL OBSERVABLE, THROUGH THE LETHALITY THAT IS REALLY THERE.** The mutant
inserts a sweep and leaves the tail one, so on a board where the COST kills — D325's Conkeldurr at
200 damage paying three {F} — the early sweep Knocks the retreater Out and parks the game on the
opponent's Prize decision **before the Ability has fired**. `selfScalingHp.test.ts` §8 drives three
rows on that board: `ABILITY_TRIGGERED{Lava Zone}` precedes `KNOCKED_OUT`, the burn lands on the
PROMOTED body with no `COUNTERS_PLACED` row anywhere, and a Magcargo-less control keeps the two
"it fired" assertions from passing on an absence. **The board D328 asked for cannot exist; the row
is killable anyway, and no amount of re-reading the declaration would have said so — only reading
the CARD did.**

**(2) `D328-ko-cascade-inherits-the-attack-cause` IS A STALE-SURVIVOR TOO, AND THE HARNESS REPORTED
IT ITSELF.** Probed individually against the FULL suite it came back `STALE-SURVIVOR — It was
KILLED. That reason has stopped being true`. The declaration was a TRUE claim about the suites
(*"the only cascade any suite builds is the Stadium one — a MID-TURN sweep, which passes no
`attackerSeat` on ANY pass, so both readings agree there"*) offered as a claim about what could be
built, and the board needed no card the suite lacked: `fix-sniper`'s Spread Shot finishes a
Ludicolo at 150 damage under its own +40 (180), and the benched Basic it was holding up sits at 55
+ the spread's 20 = 75 — alive at 100 and lethal at 60 the instant the source leaves play. D326's
marks are the reader, one of the three the declaration itself named: `byAttack: true` on the
Active, **`byAttack: false`** on the cascade victim, one action, one batch. The Stadium cascade is
kept beside it as the control the declaration correctly identified.

🛑 **THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO DECLARATIONS IS WORTH THE LINES.** The first rested on a false
claim about a CARD and could never have been right; the second rested on a true claim about the
SUITES, which stopped being true the moment a suite built another cascade. **A declaration keyed to
the catalog rots when you misread it; a declaration keyed to the test corpus rots when anyone adds
a test.** Neither rots loudly, and the exactly-once discipline caught the second only because the
`--only … --full` probe was run at all.

**(3) THE §14 TIE GUARD'S "KNOWN EDGE" WAS A WRONG ANSWER, NOT A COARSER ONE.** D328 iterated
`collectKnockOuts` to a fixed point, left the tie guard PER PASS, and wrote the gap down honestly:
*"a tie that only exists ACROSS passes still falls through to the stage-by-stage §14 checks, which
is where this function's own doc block already sends every non-speculated case"*. ⚠️ **THOSE CHECKS
CANNOT REPORT A TIE.** `resolvePrizesAndResume` evaluates §14 after EACH prize stage, so whichever
seat's stage is queued first empties its row first and wins OUTRIGHT — the sequential resolution is
*precisely what the speculation exists to pre-empt*, so sending a tie to it is sending it to the
one place that cannot express it.

One Gravity Mountain reaches the board: a Stage 2 dies on each side (pass 0 — both seats, so the
guard ran, saw a ONE-SIDED win and correctly fell through) and the dying Ludicolo's aura cascades
onto a benched teammate whose Prize is the other seat's last (pass 1). Both rows empty in one
instant; the engine answered **`win p1`**. `hpAura.test.ts` §11 drives it and was watched to fail
with exactly that, with a one-row-empties control beside it.

⚠️ **THE SPECULATION GOT SIMPLER BY MOVING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING.** Run once over
the ACCUMULATED batch, every Knock Out has already happened for real — so nothing is re-applied to
a throwaway state and only the batch's OWED PRIZES are speculative, a closer model of what the
stage path would do than replaying the KOs was. `collectKnockOutPass` loses its outcome arm
entirely and reports the seats it took a body from. **A guard that was hard to widen was hard
because it was in the wrong place.**

⚠️ **AND THE CAVEAT BECOMES AN INVARIANT: A TIE IS MONOTONE IN KNOCK OUTS.** `evaluateWin` sets a
seat's reason on an empty Prize row or on the opponent having no Pokémon in play; a later pass only
removes bodies and only adds owed prizes, so neither term can go from true back to false. A tie
visible after any prefix of the passes is still a tie after all of them — so ONE check at the end
is not weaker than a check per pass, and the later passes may add Knock Outs to a decided game,
which is §8.1's own simultaneity rather than a change of answer. Termination is untouched (the loop
is unchanged, `MAX_KO_PASSES` still its stated bound) and pass 0 still solely carries
`attackerSeat`/`attackerUid`.

### 2026-08-13 — build session #268 (P3-M5 — D328, five code-review findings, all five real, and the one shape three of them shared)

**A REVIEW-FIX SESSION, NOT A BUILD SLICE.** No new printing, no new op, no new field, no new
event, no registry row; `packages/schema` takes a zero diff. Five findings were handed over as
reasoning over code rather than as failing tests — the suite was GREEN at 335 files / 6,826
tests at the inherited head, and it was green with every one of these defects in it. **ALL FIVE
WERE REAL**, and each was driven on a board and WATCHED TO FAIL before anything was changed.

🛑 **THE SHAPE THREE OF THEM SHARE, STATED FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONLY GENERAL THING HERE.**
Recent slices added new ways for a body's EFFECTIVE MAX HP or its DAMAGE ROUTING to change
mid-turn — D316/D317 re-homed a whole main hit into a gate's arm, D324 gave the Stadium zone a
signed `hpDelta` and the seat a `seatHpBonus`, D325 made two grants shrink with the Energy count
— and **every one of them was landed without re-auditing the sites that answer "is anything
Knocked Out now".** Nothing about that is a coding mistake; each slice reasoned carefully about
its own arithmetic. What none of them did was ask the inverted question: *what ELSE reads the
number I just made movable.*

⚠️ **AND THE FIX IS THREE CALL SITES OF ONE EXISTING CHOKE POINT, NOT A NEW ABSTRACTION.** The
choke point already exists and is already right: `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts` (flow.ts) for
"something changed mid-turn, sweep", `collectKnockOuts` beneath it for the batch. A shared guard
in front of all of them would have had to be called from the same places anyway, so it would
have bought a layer and no coverage. What was missing was **call sites and a fixed point**, and
that is what was added.

**(1) THE RE-HOMED MAIN HIT WALKED PAST BOTH §9 REACTIONS — the live regression, and the one
that was fixed and pushed first.** D316's `optional` and D317's `conditionGate`/`coinFlipGate`
readers force `scaledBase` to 0 and re-home the WHOLE main hit — on BOTH gate arms — into a
`damageDefender` nested inside the gate they build. That is right for the arithmetic (§8.5
applied once, to the number the answer decided; both those suites drive it on a −30 Resistance
board) and it also stops `attack.ts` entering `if (scaledBase + scaledTotal > 0)` — the ONLY
place that seeded the defender's `damageAttacker` RECOIL (Rocky Helmet `sv01-193`, Counterattack
Quills, Custom Trap, D152's installed half) and the `onDamagedByAttack` STAGE (Armarouge
`sv03-044` "Scorching Armor", Klawf ex `sv03-120` "Counterattacking Pincer"). **All 11 legal
printings, every use, both arms** — and Chien-Pao ex's `programDamage` route had taken the same
ending since long before either.

The repair puts the seeding **at the damage instead of at one code path**: `snipeActive`
(interpreter.ts) is the interpreter's ONE §8.5 funnel for attack damage to the opponent's ACTIVE
— `placeSnipe` damages the Bench and only the Bench, and neither printed sentence is a Bench
sentence — so both reactions are applied there under the same two gates `attack.ts` uses,
`dealt > 0` and `invokedBy === "attack"`. ⚠️ **THE TRIGGER STAGE IS SPLICED IN FRONT OF THE
`koToolTrigger`/`attackEpilogue` TAIL, NOT APPENDED**, which is the one thing the shape of
`pending` makes easy to get wrong: appending is what every other stage producer does, and it
would run the reaction AFTER the §8.1 sweep the printed *"even if this Pokémon is Knocked Out"*
exists to survive. Only a LETHAL board can tell the two apart, which is why the driver has one.

**(2) THE STADIUM ZONE OWED §8.1 A SWEEP — AND D324 HAD PINNED THE GAP AS INTENDED.** The pin
reads *"the Stadium does NOT sweep on the play, and that is a call-site fact"*, and it is a TRUE
STATEMENT ABOUT THE CODE offered as a statement about the RULES. §8.1's Knock Out is a state
check on `damage ≥ maximum`, not an event of whatever moved the number; D324's own `hpDelta`
made the Stadium zone a max-HP term and Gravity Mountain `sv08-177`/`sv08-250` the engine's
FIRST subtrahend. A Stage 2 already past its reduced maximum is Knocked Out when the card lands
— exactly as a charmed Basic dies when it evolves out of Bravery Charm's clause, **which is the
analogy D324's own pin names and then decides against.** A REPLACEMENT is the same event
(discarding a Lively Stadium takes +30 off every Basic), so the sweep is owed on the PLAY, never
on the delta's sign. `SEATS` and not `[actorSeat]`, which is where this site differs from
turn.ts's three: all three legal printings read *"both yours and your opponent's"*.

⚠️ **THE PIN COULD NOT HAVE GONE RED FOR THE REASON IT CLAIMED, AND THAT IS THE LESSON RATHER
THAN THE VERDICT.** Its board carried 130 damage against a NEW maximum of 150 — a body that
survives under BOTH readings. So the assertion it actually made was *"a non-lethal drop does not
end the turn"*, which is true and always was. It is **REWRITTEN, NOT DELETED**: kept verbatim as
the non-lethal CONTROL it always was, with three lethal drivers added beside it (own board,
opponent's board, and a replacement that removes a +HP aura). **A PIN ON A BOARD THAT CANNOT
REACH THE CLAIM IS A PIN ON A DIFFERENT CLAIM.**

**(3) THE RETREAT COST COULD LEAVE A LETHALLY-DAMAGED BODY STANDING — the seam D325 RECORDED
AND REFUSED TO CLAIM.** That slice wrote, in its own suite, *"whether a sweep runs on that path
is the open seam D324 recorded for Gravity Mountain on the play, and this slice does not close
it"*, and declined to assert a Knock Out on a premise it had not verified. **The refusal was
right and the answer was no.** `hpBonus.requiresEnergyType` (Okidogi `sv06-111`/`sv06.5-074`/
`sv08.5-057` "Adrena-Power") and `hpBonusPer.attachedEnergy` (Conkeldurr `sv10.5b-049`/

maximum is at 200 under 140 the moment it pays three {F}, and it walked to the Bench and stood
there until the Checkup — healable, evolvable, gustable out of a Knock Out §8.1 had already
decided. Every OTHER discard-from-play route is an interpreter op and already folds through
`settleProgram`'s sweep; the retreat was the one that did not. The sweep sits BEHIND
`runActiveBenchedTriggers`, so the counters Lava Zone places on the body that just moved are
covered by the same interrupt rather than by a second one.

**(4) THE KO BATCH WAS A SNAPSHOT, AND IT OWED A FIXED POINT.** `collectKnockOuts` took
`lethalRefs` ONCE per batch — sound only while a Knock Out could not change any OTHER body's
lethality, which was an accident of the catalog rather than a rule until D324's `seatHpBonus`
(Ludicolo `sv09-037` "Vibrant Dance", +40 to that player's WHOLE side). Knock the source out and
every teammate loses 40 max HP in the same instant; one already past the reduced number is
Knocked Out by the same state check, and nothing re-scanned.

⚠️ **THE TERMINATION ARGUMENT IS A STRICTLY DECREASING FINITE MEASURE, AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN
BESIDE THE LOOP.** A pass runs only on a non-empty `lethalRefs`, and every ref it finds is a body
`knockOut` REMOVES from play — the Active spot is emptied, a benched body is spliced out — so
each pass strictly decreases the number of Pokémon in play. That count starts at most
`2 × (1 + BENCH_MAX)` and cannot grow inside the function: promotions are QUEUED as stages,
never run. `MAX_KO_PASSES` states the same bound as a hard stop, so a future op that DOES refill
mid-sweep turns a correctness bug into a wrong answer rather than a hang. The §14 tie guard
stays PER PASS — a widening rather than a regression, since a cascade was previously not seen at
all — and only the FIRST pass carries `attackerSeat`/`attackerUid`, because a cascade Knock Out
is caused by the maximum MOVING and not by the attack's damage.

**(5) THE HUD's CONFIRM VERB WAS A TERNARY, SO D307's `evolve` READ "TAKE 1".** Cosmetic, and
it is **D222's rule arriving on a client-side reader**. `ChooseCardsDialog` decided its label
with one `===` test per branch — `dest === "deck" ? "Shuffle" : "Take"` and
`dest === "deckBottom" ? "Put under deck" : "Discard"` — so every other member of the union fell
out of the wrong side, and TWO members were added after those lines were written: D307's
`"evolve"` (rendering *"Take 1"* over a heading reading *"…and put it onto Pidove to evolve
it"*) and D294's `"bench"` (rendering *"Discard 1/1"* for a card going onto the opponent's
Bench, and *"Take N"* for one going under their deck). `CHOOSE_CARDS_VERB` is a **TOTAL RECORD
keyed on the union**, so the next member breaks `tsc` instead of quietly inheriting a verb. Two
cells are unreachable today and are filled anyway: guessing a verb for a cell nobody can reach
is cheap, and **leaving it to a fallback is exactly how `evolve` got "Take"**.

Fifteen rows over the two halves of the seam: **NINE at the FOLD** in continuous.ts and

because a figure that was true when it was written is still a figure that has to be re-run. 🛑 **THE ACCIDENTAL SWEEP FOUND ONE GAP AND IT WAS THIS
SLICE'S SHARPEST ROW.** `D325-any-energy-becomes-a-count` swapped `hasAttachedEnergy(…)`
for `countAttachedEnergy(…) > 0` at the fold and claimed the four-{D} board separated
them. It SURVIVED — and D324's rule says a survivor is two hypotheses, a suite gap or a
row aimed at the wrong thing. **It was the second, and the reading is not a judgement
call**: `hasAttachedEnergy` is `.some(providesEnergyType)` and `countAttachedEnergy` is
`.filter(providesEnergyType).length`, so `count > 0` collapses straight back to `.some`.
A **TAUTOLOGICAL** equivalent on every board that can ever exist, and
`countAttachedEnergy`'s own docblock says so out loud (*"it must give the same answer on
the same board"*).

⚠️ **AND IT IS NOT DECLARED `survives`, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** A declaration
is a TRIPWIRE — `STALE-SURVIVOR` fails the run the day its reason stops being true — and
**a tautology can never go stale**, so declaring it would be exactly the vacuous guard
`conventions.md` forbids (*"an unreachable survivor is REMOVED, not tested around"*).
D322's melt-away row is the contrast and the reason the distinction matters: that one is
equivalent only while every `unitsOf` arm returns a non-empty array, so its declaration
really can expire. **NARROWED, NEVER RELAXED** — moved to the one place where *"any"* and
*"for each"* are two different programs, which is the ROW rather than the reader:
`D325-okidogi-authored-as-a-per-energy-scale` keys the +100 on Conkeldurr's scale and §2's
four-{D} board reads 530 instead of 230. **KILLED.**

## 🛑 THE TOOLING FINDING, AND IT COST THIS SLICE ITS WORST HALF-HOUR

**THERE IS NO `--precheck` FLAG.** `bun run mutants -- --precheck` **SILENTLY RAN THE
ENTIRE 804-ROW CORPUS** — the runner parses `--list`, `--only`, `--decision`, `--full`,
`--verbose` and `--allow-dirty` and **ignores everything else without a word**.
`precheck` is a SEPARATE entry point, **`bun scripts/mutation/precheck.ts`**, and it
answers in one second. The header line the runner prints is the only warning, and piping
it through `tail` hid it for the whole run. **AN INHERITED RATIONALE IS A CLAIM — AND SO
IS AN INHERITED COMMAND LINE.**

⚠️ **THE RUN WAS NOT KILLED, AND THAT IS THE OTHER HALF.** D324's worst hour came from
killing one and pushing a live mutant past `tsc` and `biome`. The harness **REFUSES to
write to a dirty file** (`skipped(dirty)`) rather than clobbering it, so **letting a
wrong run finish is almost always cheaper than killing it**. It ended normally, the tree
was verified clean of mutants afterwards, and its ONE `skipped(dirty)` was
`D275-engine-version-drifts-again` on the then-uncommitted `index.ts` — closed by the
clean sweep. ⚠️ **AND `bunx tsc -b` IS BLIND TO `scripts/mutation/mutants.ts`**: a
generator bug left fifteen rows with unescaped inner quotes and the type gate was GREEN
on the broken file. **A CORPUS EDIT IS GATED BY RUNNING THE HARNESS, NEVER BY THE TYPE
CHECKER.**

## 🛑 THE DRY RUN CAUGHT A PAGE-EATING DOCS EDIT

D323 instituted the scratchpad dry run of the `progress.md` script, and it paid here in a
way no assertion in the script itself would have. The status-row replacement was first
spelled `re.search(r"\| simulator \| P3 \|.*?\|\n", s, flags=re.S)`. **With `re.S` the
`.*?` crosses newlines**, and the pattern matched a PROSE mention of the row inside the
session log, then ran **582,003 characters** to the next `|\n`. Committed, that is
**D317's 2,014-line deletion in a different costume** — and every one of the script's own
guards (the archive count at 38 on both sides, the resume-point newline anchor) would
have passed, because the damage was in a region none of them look at. The fix is a
LINE-ANCHORED, non-DOTALL `findall` plus an assertion that it matches **exactly once**.
**A REGEX THAT CAN CROSS A NEWLINE IS A REGEX THAT CAN EAT A DOCUMENT — ANCHOR IT TO A
LINE AND COUNT THE MATCHES.**

## 🛑 A PROHIBITION IS NOT A CLAMPED REDUCTION, AND `count === 0` WOULD HAVE MERGED THEM

Glimmora's heads prints *"your opponent **can't take any** Prize cards for it"* — a PROHIBITION,
which a later permission does not overturn — so a denied Knock Out takes no bonus **and does not
even flip Wonder Kiss's coin**. A REDUCTION clamped to 0 is a different sentence: Munkidori ex says
*"1 fewer"*, nothing forbids the taking, and a bonus on top of it is arithmetic. Both are driven on
real boards (`fix-koprize` is the 1-Prize body with a constructed `by: 2` D164 built for exactly
that line). **A build that keyed the refusal on `count === 0` would collapse the two and hand the
prohibition's answer to the clamp** — and this file had already drawn that distinction once, in
`PRIZE_PREVENTED` vs `PRIZE_REDUCED`.

first"*. The converse is now paid for too: **a row listed as DONE is also a claim about the

both HUDs — derived this row part by part, and then wrote *"⚠️ **DO NOT

on trust would have shipped a defect.**

⚠️ **THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOT THAT D314 WAS CARELESS — IT READ MORE CODE THAN MOST
SLICES DO.** It is that **a derivation names WHAT IS MISSING, and "missing" is a
claim about the whole codebase that no amount of reading the FAMILY can settle.**
Both errors have that shape: one says a mechanism must be authored per-CARD when
the family authors it per-SENTENCE; the other says a predicate does not exist when
it exists twice, one op set over. 🛑 **THE OPERATIONAL FORM: A HANDOFF MAY PRICE
WHAT IT *READ*; IT MAY NEVER PRICE WHAT IT *DID NOT FIND*.** When you inherit a
derivation, re-run the two cheapest queries against it — *how do this family's
SIBLINGS pay for themselves?* and *`git grep` the predicate you are told is
missing* — before writing a line. Both came back against the handoff in under ten
minutes.

**✅ WHAT THE HANDOFF GOT RIGHT IS THE SHAPE, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING HALF.**
ONE new `EffectOp` (`evolveFromDeckEachChosen`), ONE `stepOp` arm, ONE
do-nothing `applyChoice` arm, and **`continuationOps`' FOURTH member — the FIRST
to answer a `pokemonMulti` and the FIRST whose answer buys *N* ops rather than
one.** `optional` (D186) answers a `confirm`; `moveCountersChosen` (D216) and

Every other `choosePokemonMulti` in this engine — `damageChosen`,
`healChosen.upTo` — is applied in `applyChoice` and buys BOARD CHANGES, which is

AS NARROW AS ITS COLUMNS, ITS LITERAL *AND ITS WORD ORDER* — AND ONLY THE THIRD
RESISTS BEING FIXED MECHANICALLY.** Widening a column set is a procedure. Shortening
a literal to the part a pronoun cannot change is a procedure, and D311 wrote it down
as the operational form. Neither procedure can imagine that English says the same
thing backwards; the only instrument that reaches it is reading the printed sentence
for what it could have said instead of what the query assumed it said.

**🛑 THE SEAM AT ITS SECOND SITE — PRICED FROM THE CODE, AND IT IS NOT MORE
EXPENSIVE.** D311 proved the §8.1 promotion is a QUEUEING SEAM rather than a stage
and put one in `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts`, which serves `settleProgram` — Trainers,
Abilities, board triggers. `finishAttack` calls `collectKnockOuts` **directly** and
never passes through it, so an attack that removes its own actor handed the turn
over with an empty Active Spot. The brief asked whether the second site is genuinely
more expensive. **It is not, and the evidence is the diff:**

    resolveMidTurnKnockOuts   [...batch.stages, ...orphaned, resumeTurn]
    finishAttack              [...batch.stages, ...orphaned, ...turnTail]

Same filter, same `.map`, same `PendingStage {kind:"promote"}` — which gained
nothing and is still total over its three boards (pops on a refilled spot,
auto-resolves a Bench of one, falls into the §14.2 loss on a Bench of none).

of, and the difference is what makes each one correct**: an Ability does not end a
turn (§9) so the actor RESUMES; an attack does (§5.3) and §8.1 owes the promotion
BEFORE it, because a player does not hand over a board with an empty Active Spot.
That ORDER is the only thing about this site that could have been got wrong, and it
is driven rather than argued — `TURN_ENDED` must not have fired while the promotion
is still queued, and a mutant that splices the stages BEHIND `turnTail` reddens on
exactly that rung.

**The effect string is byte-identical across all six.** The names differ, the
`damage` fields differ, the Stage differs — none of which the reader-keyed
summand sees. That is the whole mechanism behind the 4 + 2.

**REFUSED, and the refusal's TYPE changes from a rule to a return channel.** The
standing prose said *"it evolves, which the interpreter must never do"*. Read
rather than repeated, what actually stands in the way is **COMPOSITION**:

* `stepOp` (interpreter.ts) returns
  `{ done: GameState; schedule?: EffectOp[] } | { park: EffectPrompt }`, and
  `runProgram` returns `done | parked`. An op hands back a bare state or a prompt.
* `placeEvolution` (turn.ts) — the one function in the engine that puts an
  evolution card on a stack, shared by `evolve` and Rare Candy — ends in one of
  two `ApplyResult` calls, **both of which set a phase**, and this slice
  **DRIVES BOTH on real boards**: `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts` seeds `state.pending`
  (a charmed Basic dropping under its Stage 2's HP → `ko:takePrizes`), and
  `runBoardTrigger(…, "onEvolve", …)` folds through `settleProgram` and **PARKS**
  (Arboliva `sv01-023` "Enriching Oil" → `effect:choose`).

⚠️ **And the two halves are not equally expensive, which is the pricing nobody
had done.** In an ATTACK context the KO tail is nearly free — the attack ends the
turn anyway (§5.3) and `finishAttack` already sweeps the ATTACKER's own board, so
"resume the actor's turn" has nothing to resume. **The TRIGGER tail has no cheap
answer**: an on-evolve program parking inside an attack-effect program is a park
inside a park, and `EffectContinuation` holds exactly one `pendingOp`.

**Three stale claims in the card's own doc block, corrected.** It presented the
sentence as Exeggcute's (it is 2 of 6); it enumerated `dest` as *"hand / bench /
discard / …"* when a registry-wide walk over every authored op returns exactly
**`{bench, hand}`** — a stale third member that made the widening look cheaper
than it is; and it typed the blocker as the rule rather than as the channel.
**A parenthetical enumerating a union is the cheapest kind of doc claim to check
and nobody had.**

### 2026-08-09 — build session #245 (P3-M5 — D305, the `ability` column's 215 ids, and the card count is the JOIN)

**Slice.** D304's method applied one column over, in the order D304 prescribed:
registry object grouping FIRST (`programFor` identity over `CENSUS_POKEMON_LEGAL`'s
215 ids), and only then `COUNT(DISTINCT name)` against remote D1 `luminous`. The
reverse order cannot find what this found — the catalog does not know which
printings this repo binds to one object.

**D304's flagged clause HOLDS, and the reasoning under it is backwards.** D304
flagged *"the `ability` column has at least one name/body collision of D304's
kind"* as its most-likely-wrong claim, arguing that `abilities_json` sentences are
long and card-specific so the collision might be *"STRUCTURALLY RARE OR IMPOSSIBLE
one column over"*. There are **EIGHT** colliding objects here against `trainer`'s
**ONE**, covering **34 of the 215 printings**, and the largest — `COPPERAJAH_EX` —
is shared by **FIVE distinct cards** (Tangrowth, Dubwool, Cetitan, Mudsdale,
Bouffalant ex) across 8 printings.

**The finding is about the INSTRUMENT rather than about this column.**

    215 printings  →  82 program objects  →  92 distinct names  →  94 CARDS

D304's method returns TWO numbers (82 and 92) and **neither is the card count**.
The card count is the **JOIN** — distinct `(name, program object)` pairs — and it
is **larger than both**, because the two failures run in opposite directions and
neither subsumes the other: 8 objects carry more than one NAME, and **2 NAMES span
more than one OBJECT** (`Carracosta`, `Crustle` — two different cards sharing a
name and printing different Abilities). That converse does not occur on the
`trainer` column at all. **`Crustle` is in BOTH lists at once**, which is exactly
why neither number can be patched into the other. *A partition and a
`COUNT(DISTINCT …)` are two projections of a join, and a projection cannot be
audited by another projection.*

**The `NEMONA` pathology is systematic here.** Three of the 8 colliding objects are
named for pre-SV cards in no column at all (`COPPERAJAH_EX`, `STONJOURNER`,
`COUNTERATTACK_QUILLS`), and `COPPERAJAH_EX` is sharper than `NEMONA`: a card
actually named `Copperajah` (`sv06.5-042`) **is** in this column and does **not**
use it — it prints "Massive Body" on its own program.

**And one constant is named for an Ability that does not exist.**
`CURIOUS_TEA_PARTY`'s doc block, field doc, three binding comments and four
test-file headers all described *"Poltchageist / Sinistcha `sv10-048` 'Curious Tea
Party'"*, *"an evolution LINE plus a reprint"*. Every clause is false:
`instr(abilities_json,'Curious Tea Party') > 0` returns **ZERO rows over all 3,786**
(Poltchageist's Ability is **"Storehouse Hideaway"**); **`sv10-048` is `Misty's
Magikarp`** ("So Submerged", `evolve_from` **NULL**); and the real `Sinistcha` is
**`sv06-022`** (`evolve_from = 'Poltchageist'`, `legal_standard = 1`), which is not
in `registry.ts` at all. ⚠️ **The BINDING was correct the whole time** — the three
printings do share one sentence and the count of 3 is right — **only the names were
wrong, which is why D254's re-derivation of the COUNT could not catch it.** That is
D303's rule from a third side, and the third consecutive column whose rot was in
the names rather than the arithmetic. Corrected at 9 sites; the constant NAME is
left in place deliberately, as `NEMONA` was at D304.

**The three-column key is NOT a no-op here — it is the exact inverse of D304's
reading.** Over these 215: `abilities_json` **202**, `attacks_json` **215**,
`effect` **ZERO**. A census keyed on `effect` alone — the single-column shape this
page used for thirty-four slices — **would have returned nothing at all**. The
13-row shortfall is exactly the `attackGate` cohort (`215 − 202 = 13`), and the 13
ids the catalog says carry no Ability are the same 13 whose registry program has an
`attackGate` key — asserted in both directions. **So D304 was right to retire the
caution for `trainer` and it would have been a disaster as a general rule: "run it
or drop it" must be run PER COLUMN.**

**Deliverable.** `ABILITY_NAME_TERMS` — 92 `[name, printings]` rows summing to 215

by object identity; the 8 collisions named with their 34-printing population and

**A guard nobody had met caught this slice's own prose.** `catalogManifest.test.ts`'s
*"finds no count that no query produced"* went red on the phrase **"3,786 cards"**

allowlist.

(`{kind:"upTo"}`), which is the one mode these four do not print. The paragraph D295
read is TRUE of the op it is printed on and silent about the union member beside it.
🛑 **A CONTRACT WRITTEN ON ONE OP IS NOT A CONTRACT ABOUT THE SENTENCE.**

**BUILT — 4 legal printings on 3 sentences, all attacks.** Octillery `sv09-034` "Aqua
Wash" ({W}, 20, *"You may put an Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon into
their hand."*); Unfezant `sv05-135` "Opposing Winds" ({C}{C}, 70) and Slowking

with its `conditionHolds` and `conditionNote` arms. **No new op, no new prompt kind, no
new choice kind, no new event, no error code, no registry row**; `packages/schema`,

is D262's predicate reused VERBATIM — that slice wrote it with the warning that

Stage 2 gate sits **outside** the "may", inverting the printed word order: the adjective
is a board fact settled before anybody is asked, so gating inside would park a Yes/No
whose YES is a guaranteed no-op on every board it excludes. ⚠️ **THE FIRST BUILD HAD IT
THE OTHER WAY ROUND AND THE DOC COMMENT ALREADY SAID OTHERWISE** — the code was written
`optional{conditionGate{…}}` while the block above it argued for the opposite — and the
§5 Stage-1 case is what caught it. *A doc comment written in the same commit as the code
it describes is not evidence the code obeys it.* **A MEASURED CONSEQUENCE**: because the
gate resolves and splices before anything parks, **the new `BoardCondition` member can
never appear in a `MatchRecord` at all**, which is a stronger claim than *"adding an
inhabitant owes no bump"* and is asserted as a `not.toContain` on the serialized phase.

WRONG FUNCTION.** It doubted that Lickitung's *"interchangeable collapse"* blocker was

🛑 **A WINDOW IS NOT A PREDICATE YOU CAN WIDEN.**

**THE REFUSAL'S CONCLUSION HELD AND ONE HALF OF ITS STATED REASON DID NOT.**

arithmetic before the field; here **there is no arithmetic** — the bar is
installed by an attack that has already resolved, §5.3 ends the turn immediately

that field records a turn that has PASSED and this one a turn that is COMING, and
both make the window fall out of arithmetic rather than out of a clear. Per-CLASS
because the pool prints both values of the slot, and **a single "locked" boolean
would let a Budew bar the Supporter its sentence does not mention** — which is
one of the seven mutants.

### 2026-08-08 — build session #217 (P3-M5 — D276, one structural program walker, five hand-rolled copies retired)

**D276 — THE SLICE WITH NO PRINTED CARD, BECAUSE BOTH INHERITED CLAIMS TURNED OUT
MIS-STATED AND ONE OF THEM WAS HIDING SOMETHING BIGGER.**

**PART A — D265's UNNAMED "BLOCKED ON OTHER MACHINERY" IS REAL, AND ITS NAME IS
CROSS-SEAT PUT-INTO-PLAY.** The handoff was explicit that this phrase must be
re-derived rather than inherited, because D275 had just caught an inherited price
that was too HIGH. It is not too high here. Mandibuzz `sv10.5w-064`/`-145` *"Look
for Prey"* — *"Once during your turn, you may use this Ability. Your opponent
reveals their hand, and you put a Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less that you find
there onto your **opponent's** Bench."* — both ids re-queried alone
(`legal_standard = 1`, `category = 'Pokemon'`, `hp = 110`,
`types_json = ["Darkness"]`, one byte-identical `abilities_json`), so the
2-printings-on-one-sentence clause is measured and not inherited either.

✅ **THE PREDICTION THAT THE `maxHp` HALF COSTS ZERO IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND SO IS
"THE PRICE IS IN THE OP, NOT THE FILTER."** *"a Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or
less"* is `basicPokemon.maxHp: 70` — D265's own rider at D265's own threshold,
shipped since Buddy-Buddy Poffin, verbatim.

🛑 **THE OP IS A CAPABILITY THIS ENGINE DOES NOT HAVE, MEASURED BY READING THE
MOVERS RATHER THAN BY ARGUING.** `searchMove` and `retrieveMove` are the ONLY two
functions that put a card into play — `makeInPlay` is reached through nothing
else — and both hard-code `ctx.seat`'s own zones on both ends. The nearest
neighbour owns everything except the destination: `bottomFromOpponentHand` (D232)
already reveals the opponent's hand through the shared `revealHand`, filters it
through `matchesFilter`, collapses interchangeable copies, parks the mandatory
`chooseCards` and moves a card **inside the opponent's zones** — and then ends at
`deck: [...side.deck, ...moved]`.

⚠️ **AND A DESTINATION IS NOT A RIDER HERE, WHICH IS THE PART A PER-ROW PRICE
CANNOT SEE.** The park's `dest` union — `"bench" | "hand" | "deck" | "deckBottom"
| "discard"` — means *your* bench at every one of its readers. An opponent-side
bench crosses `redact.ts`, a `z.enum` in `packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts`
and TWO `src/` HUDs (`GameHud.tsx`, `OnlineHud.tsx`): a schema boundary and an app
diff, not a registry row. **REFUSED, AND NAMED** — per the standing rule, and per
the handoff's own instruction to take a named alternative rather than force the
row.

**PART B — THE NAMED ALTERNATIVE, AND THE FLAGGED GAP WAS THE WRONG ONE.** The
handoff offered `tailsGatedOp.test.ts`'s `.otherwise` sweep gap and told me to
READ IT BEFORE PREDICTING A COUNT, hedging that it *"may be STRUCTURALLY
INCAPABLE of reddening, which is itself the answer to record."*

🛑 **IT IS. `coinFlipGate.otherwise` OCCURS ZERO TIMES** across `FIXTURE_POOL` and
the whole registry, so closing that arm alone could not have changed a single
answer. D269 flagged it, D270–D275 each carried it forward, and it was true in the
TYPE and vacuous in the POOL the entire time.

⚠️ **BUT THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVED IT FOUND A LIVE GAP NOBODY HAD NAMED, AND IT
WAS IN FIVE SUITES AT ONCE.** A structural walk over the same corpus finds **402**
ops where `tailsGatedOp`'s enumerated walk finds **398**. The entire difference is
**`optional.then`**: `fix-trainerops` attack 10's `opponentSwitchOut`, and
`fix-rapidvernier`'s trigger hiding a `switchActive`, a `recordGate`, and a
`moveEnergy` one level deeper inside that gate.

🛑 **FIVE AUDITORS EACH CARRIED THEIR OWN COPY OF ONE RECURSION AND EACH
ENUMERATED A DIFFERENT SUBSET OF THE FOUR BRANCHING OPS.**

| suite | walker | branches descended |
|---|---|---|
| `preventBlock.test.ts` | `walkKinds` | all four |
| `vengefulPunch.test.ts` | `walk` | three (no `optional`) |
| `tailsGatedOp.test.ts` | `walk` | three (no `optional`) |
| `attackDebuff.test.ts` | `walk` | **two**, chained through `else if` |
| `preventBlock.test.ts` | the `invokedBy`/`source` agreement | **one** |

`attackDebuff`'s missed a producer inside a gate TWICE over — once for the
undescended branch, and once because an `else if` chain means a gate op can never
fall through to the producer arm even when the walk does reach it.

🛑 **AND `walkKinds`'S OWN DOC BLOCK RECORDS THE SAME DEFECT BEING FOUND AND
PATCHED FIVE SEPARATE TIMES** — D148 (`conditionGate`), D150 (`recordGate`), D227
(`optional`) — always one arm at a time, always *after* a fixture happened to
print the shape that exposed the previous omission. Each patch closed the hole the
pool had just reached and left the next one open. **THAT IS NOT FIVE MISTAKES; IT
IS ONE MISSING ABSTRACTION**, which is D275's *"a debt paid N times is a missing
guard, not a recurring mistake"* applied to an auditor rather than to a constant.

🛑 **WHY IT SURVIVED: THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION.** A
sweep that misses a branch does not throw. It returns a SMALLER SET, and every
`expect(...).toEqual([...])` over it goes GREEN — because the row that would have
broken the assertion is the row the walk never reached. A guard that under-reports
looks exactly like a guard with nothing to report.

✅ **THE FIX IS A NEGATIVE PREDICATE, WHICH IS THE STANDING RULE ARRIVING EXACTLY
WHERE IT WAS OWED.** `walkProgram` (testFixtures.ts) never asks WHICH op it is
looking at: a sub-program is any array-valued property whose elements are objects
carrying a string `op` — the shape of an `EffectOp[]` and of nothing else in the
union. **No key list** (a future third branch name costs nothing) and **no op
list** (a sixth gate is swept the day it is authored, not the day someone
notices). The enumerated thing here — the set of branching ops — GROWS with the
union, which is precisely the standing rule's trigger condition.

✅ **`programBranchCarriers` IS THE AUDITOR OVER THE PREDICATE, AND THE
DISTINCTION MATTERS.** `walkProgram` is deliberately blind to what it descends, so
nothing inside it can notice the union grew a fifth branching op. This is the
thing that notices, and it fails NAMING the op and the property rather than by
quietly sweeping less. Its pin reads `coinFlipGate ["then"]`,
`conditionGate ["otherwise","then"]`, `optional ["then"]`, `recordGate ["then"]` —
and that `coinFlipGate` row is the recorded, permanent answer to D269's flag.

⚠️ **THE ONE THING THE PREDICATE CANNOT REACH IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE
FOUND** — D150's finding, kept: `deriveAttackCoinFlip`'s `programPerHeads.ops`
hangs off a COIN reading, not off an op, so no structural walk from a program root
can see it. Its caller feeds it in separately.

✅ **PROVEN RED TWO WAYS BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED, ONE CODE AND ONE DATA.**
* **CODE** — narrowing the predicate to the key `then` turns **4 cases red across
  2 suites**, including `preventBlock`'s downstream *"the sweep DESCENDS every
  gate, not only the coin."*
* **DATA** — authoring a real `coinFlipGate.otherwise` onto a shipped trainer
  program turns **2 red**, the carrier pin naming `coinFlipGate` gaining the key.

**BOTH PERTURBATIONS WERE UNDONE BY INVERSE SUBSTITUTION AND VERIFIED WITH
`git diff`** — D275's rule, and made cheap by committing the green step FIRST, so
the undo was checkable against a real HEAD rather than against memory.

🆕 **THE ENGINE VERSION DOES NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS A DECISION.** Every shipped
